docs.title: 1. Generate temporary examples
docs.text:
The suite builds projects from small YAML inputs in src/test/fixtures/. The inputs cover supported buses, languages, register layouts, and vendor options.

Generated files are temporary test output. Source templates remain under src/generator/templates/.

docs.title: 2. Validate Quartus output
docs.text:
The Quartus suite runs in Docker so contributors and CI use a consistent tool environment. It checks the generated project script and, when available, the generated bus testbench.

A bus functional model is test code that behaves like a bus controller. It sends reads and writes to the generated design so the suite can confirm that the wrapper and register logic work together.

docs.title: 3. Validate Vivado output
docs.text:
The Vivado suite starts Vivado in batch mode. It checks the generated IP package, then creates a small block design and connects the IP where applicable.

This catches problems that a text comparison cannot, including invalid interface metadata, missing clock relationships, and unsupported block-design connections.

docs.title: Why these tests run separately
docs.text:
Vendor tools are large and slow, and many contributors have only one installed. Keeping these suites separate makes the everyday unit tests fast while still providing a strong validation gate in CI.

The tests also allow individual vendor paths to be selected. A contributor who changes only Vivado output does not need to run Quartus locally.

docs.title: Failure ownership
docs.text:
Use the first failing stage to narrow the cause:

Do not repair a generated test file by hand. Change the source generator or template, rebuild, and rerun the suite.

docs.title: Main implementation areas
docs.text: Area Location Integration tests src/test/integration/ Test inputs src/test/fixtures/ Generator source src/generator/ Source templates src/generator/templates/ Integration Jest setup config/jest.integration.js

docs.title: Running the suites
docs.text: See Running the EDA integration tests for prerequisites, commands, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Generator Feature Coverage
docs.text:
This matrix records what the generator verification suites prove about generated register RTL. It is requirement coverage, not TypeScript line coverage.

The distinction between the columns matters:

  • VHDL RTL means GHDL analyzes, elaborates, and synthesizes the generated VHDL.
  • SystemVerilog RTL means Icarus compiles and Verilator lints the generated SystemVerilog.
  • Behavioral simulation means a testbench makes assertions about generated behavior. A generated cocotb test that only completes bus transactions is identified as a smoke test instead.
  • Vendor synthesis means the generated project completes Quartus compile or Vivado out-of-context synthesis. This proves tool acceptance, not register semantics.
  • Hardware requires a maintained on-board test result or log. A tutorial or manually run example without retained results is not counted.

Yes therefore means that the named evidence directly covers the row. No names a current verification gap. All fixture-based checks generate both HDL backends unless a cell says otherwise.

docs.text:
The schema defines seven AccessType values. The dedicated register-semantics testbench checks all seven against the generated daq_controller_regs module with GHDL and Icarus.

docs.title: Known Verification Gaps
docs.text:
The matrix deliberately leaves these gaps visible:

  • No maintained hardware test result is linked to the generator suite. The DE10-Nano case study describes a manual workflow, but it is not an on-board regression gate and does not preserve per-feature results.
  • Quartus synthesis does not currently cover write-only, read-write-self-clearing, register-level reset, or nested register groups.
  • Register-level reset is checked by the generated manifest scoreboard when a generated fixture includes one.
  • Vendor synthesis proves that a representative project is accepted by the tool. It does not prove reset values, readback policy, W1C/SC arbitration, monitorChangeOf, array address isolation, or byte-enable behavior.

docs.text:

The suite implementation and commands are described in How EDA integration tests work and Running the EDA integration tests.

docs.title: Port Field Metadata
docs.text:
Proposal: optional field metadata on the ports of an .ip.yml that names what the bits of a port carry. It covers top-level ports, conduit ports, and bus interface ports. It is metadata only. Generators ignore it and generated code does not change; user tools (cocotb tests, documentation, the Data Inspector) read it for their own purposes.

Status: proposal, for review (issue #287). The schema change lands in ipcraft-spec; this repository consumes it.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A packed port such as a 16-bit status word, a 64-bit command bus, or an AXI-Stream TDATA payload has an internal layout that today lives only in HDL comments or in the designer's head. Every consumer reconstructs it by hand:

Consumer What it does today cocotb testbench Hard-codes shifts and masks to drive and check sub-fields Documentation Describes the layout in prose, separately from the spec Data Inspector The user retypes the fields; only memory-map registers can be imported

Memory-map registers already have this (fields with bits, description, enumeratedValues). Ports do not.

docs.title: Field format
docs.text:
A port field uses the memory-map bit-field format, minus the two keys that only make sense for a register.

Key Required Meaning name yes Field name, unique within the port bits one position form Inclusive range "[msb:lsb]", or "[n]" for one bit offset, width one position form Start bit (LSB = 0) and number of bits, as an alternative to bits description no Free text enumeratedValues no Map {value: name}

Not included: access and resetValue. A port has no register access semantics and no reset value. Display hints such as signed or fixed-point stay in the Data Inspector recipe.

In the schema this is a new PortFieldDef with the same property definitions as BitFieldDef, so readers that already parse register fields can parse port fields with the same code.

docs.title: Where fields are declared
docs.text:
Port kind Location Key Top-level port ports[] fields: [...] Conduit port busInterfaces[].conduitPorts[] fields: [...] Bus interface port busInterfaces[] portFields: { <logicalName>: [...] }

Bus interface ports have no entry of their own in .ip.yml; they come from the bus definition. portFields is keyed by logical port name, following the existing portWidthOverrides and portNameOverrides maps, so the key stays stable when physicalPrefix or a name override changes. The layout belongs to the interface instance, not the bus definition: TDATA carries different payloads in different designs.

Clocks, resets, and interrupts are out of scope.

apiVersion: "1.2"

ports:
  - name: o_status
    direction: out
    width: 16
    description: Packed status word
    fields:
      - name: state
        bits: "[3:0]"
        description: Main FSM state
        enumeratedValues:
          0: IDLE
          1: RUN
          2: ERROR
      - name: overflow
        bits: "[4]"
        description: Sticky FIFO overflow
      - name: level
        offset: 8
        width: 8
        description: FIFO fill level in words

busInterfaces:
  - name: s_axis
    type: ipcraft:busif:axi_stream:1.0
    mode: slave
    physicalPrefix: s_axis_
    portFields:
      TDATA:
        - name: sample
          bits: "[23:0]"
          description: Signed 24-bit audio sample
        - name: channel
          bits: "[27:24]"
      TUSER:
        - name: first
          bits: "[0]"
          description: First sample of a frame

  - name: dbg
    type: ipcraft:busif:conduit:1.0
    mode: conduit
    conduitPorts:
      - name: dbg_state
        direction: out
        width: 8
        fields:
          - name: phase
            bits: "[2:0]"

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text: Rule Decision Bit numbering Bit 0 is the LSB of the HDL vector as declared. Independent of a port's endianness, which only describes byte order. Gaps Allowed. Bits not covered by a field are unused or reserved. Overlap Not allowed. A port has exactly one layout; alternative views of the same bits are a Data Inspector concern (overlay groups). Parametric width Field positions are integers. When the port width is a parameter or expression (including bus widths from the bus definition, portWidthOverrides, or a parameter), positions are checked against the width resolved with parameter defaults. Bus array interfaces portFields applies to every instance of the array. Copy, not reference A port never references a register layout. When a port mirrors a register, its fields are copied; references would create a dependency that has to be kept in sync both ways. Generators Ignore field metadata. No HDL, vendor, or cocotb output changes.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Port and BusInterface reject unknown keys, and the schema states that tools must not read a file declaring a newer apiVersion than they support. Field metadata therefore ships as apiVersion: 1.2, the new latest version, through the same upgrade mechanism as 1.1:

Path Effect Migration step 1.1 to 1.2 No content changes; only apiVersion is stamped Editor A file behind the latest version is upgraded on its first edit, so every file edited with this IPCraft declares 1.2, with or without field metadata ipcraft migrate Upgrades files to 1.2 Older IPCraft Refuses a 1.2 file with "upgrade IPCraft" instead of a schema error

The Python package in ipcraft-spec ships the schema files only, so the schema change is its whole update.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Metadata that nothing checks goes stale, so the IP core editor checks it from the first release, in a "Port fields" group of the Issues panel (src/webview/ipcore/utils/portFieldChecks.ts). All checks are warnings, never generation errors.

Check Example message Exactly one position form per field o_status.level: use bits or offset/width, not both Position inside the resolved port width o_status.level [15:8] exceeds port width 12 No overlap between fields o_status: fields state and mode overlap at bit 3 Unique field names within a port o_status: duplicate field name state Enumerated values fit the field width o_status.state: value 17 does not fit in 4 bits portFields key is a logical port of the bus definition s_axis.portFields: TKEEP2 is not a port of axi_stream portFields key is not absent or disabled s_axis.portFields: TUSER is not enabled on this interface Width not resolvable Range checks skipped, no warning

For an interface imported without a bus definition, the logical names come from rawPortMaps.

docs.title: Editor: fields follow the signal
docs.text:
Editing field metadata in the IP core UI is not part of this proposal; users write it in YAML. The editor must preserve it, including through gestures that change what kind of port a signal is:

Gesture Code Field metadata Rename, move, change width or direction of a port SignalPanels, useCanvasDrop Kept on the port Group ports into a bus interface, new or existing useGroupPorts groupAsStandard, mergePortsIntoStandardBus (mapping from GroupingMappingStep) ports[].fields moves to portFields[<logicalName>] Add one port to a bus interface useGroupPorts addPortToStandardBus ports[].fields moves to portFields[<signalName>] Group ports into a conduit, or add one useGroupPorts groupAsConduit, addPortToConduit ports[].fields moves to conduitPorts[].fields Ungroup a bus interface into ports useGroupPorts ungroupBusInterface portFields[<logicalName>] or conduitPorts[].fields moves to ports[].fields Map a conduit to a known bus applyMapConduitToKnownBus (mapping from MapConduitToBusDialog) conduitPorts[].fields moves to portFields[<logicalName>]; unmapped conduit ports keep theirs Save a conduit as a custom bus definition ConduitPanel conduitPorts[].fields moves to portFields[<conduit port name>], the logical name the saved definition uses Remove a conduit signal ConduitPanel Removed with the signal Disable an optional bus port IpBlockCanvas portFields entry kept; the validator warns that the port is not enabled

The physical-to-logical mapping comes from the dialog that already knows it, the same way MapConduitToBusDialog carries a conduit port's width into portWidthOverrides. Each gesture stays one document update. Plain edits already keep field metadata (see Verification); the gestures above rebuild objects from a fixed list of keys and drop it today, so they need explicit handling plus tests.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:

docs.title: Data Inspector: Import from port
docs.text:
Tracked in issue #288.

Import copies the fields once into a recipe, like the register import; there is no live link.

Item Decision Picker Ports join the existing layout picker and the Open Register or Port in Data Inspector command, grouped as Registers and Ports. One layout reader, one message, one copy path. Source One source per imported port, width resolved with parameter defaults. Ports whose width does not resolve or exceeds 4096 bits are not offered. What is offered Ports with at least one usable field. Bus portFields keys that are unknown or not enabled are skipped, as are fields with a malformed position, a range beyond the port width, or a range that overlaps an earlier field of the same port. A key that differs from an earlier key of the same bus only in case is skipped too. Field translation bits / offset+width become the recipe's msb/lsb; enumeratedValues becomes enumValues. The display interpretation stays at its default, as for the register import. Provenance importProvenance is one of { sourceFile, registerName } or { sourceFile, portName, busInterface? }. A top-level port names only portName; a conduit port adds busInterface; a bus interface port uses the logical port name in contract casing (TDATA).

docs.title: Rejected
docs.text: Option Reason Alternative or union layouts (overlay groups on a port) No concrete benefit over one layout plus descriptions; the Data Inspector already offers overlay groups for ad hoc views. Referencing a register layout from a port Creates a dependency that has to be updated back and forth. Copy instead. Reusing BitFieldDef verbatim Would allow access and resetValue, which have no meaning on a port. bits as the only position form Register fields accept offset/width too; one format for both keeps readers simple. Using the metadata in generators (VHDL records, SV packed structs) Out of scope. If it comes, it is a separate opt-in proposal.

docs.title: Responsive Design
docs.text: IPCraft runs inside editor columns that users can resize. The layout must remain usable in a wide editor, a split editor, and a narrow side-by-side view.

docs.title: What changes with width
docs.text:
Editor width User-visible behavior Up to 640 px Memory Map outline becomes an overlay; tables use compact cards 641–900 px Outline narrows and less important columns are hidden 901 px and wider Full outline and all table columns are visible

The editor is designed for desktop use. The narrow layout supports resized VS Code panes; it is not a separate mobile application.

Wide editor Narrow editor with outline open

docs.title: Memory Map layout
docs.text:
The wide layout places the outline beside the details panel. In the narrow layout, a button opens the outline over the editor and a backdrop closes it.

The overlay must:

  • remain above table and visualizer content;
  • close when the backdrop is selected;
  • return focus to the button that opened it;
  • keep controls large enough for pointer and touch use.

docs.title: IP Core layout
docs.text: The IP Core editor contains a toolbar, library palette, canvas, and inspector. It does not use the Memory Map outline overlay. When space is limited, its panels must shrink or scroll without covering the canvas controls.

docs.title: Implementation values
docs.text:
The shared values are defined in src/webview/index.css:

CSS value Purpose --sidebar-width Wide Memory Map outline --sidebar-width-tablet Medium-width outline --sidebar-width-mobile Narrow overlay width --touch-target-min Minimum interactive control size

Colors use VS Code theme variables so the layout works in light, dark, and high-contrast themes.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
When changing layout code, check all three width ranges and confirm:

  • the selected item remains visible;
  • tables can scroll without covering headers;
  • the outline opens, closes, and returns keyboard focus;
  • visualizers remain readable;
  • labels do not overlap controls;
  • interactive controls meet the minimum target size;
  • light, dark, and high-contrast themes remain readable.

Automated browser tests should set explicit viewport sizes for behavior that depends on a breakpoint.

docs.title: Spatial Editing
docs.text:
Some IPCraft items occupy a range rather than only a list position:

  • an address block occupies addresses;
  • a register occupies bytes inside a block;
  • a bit field occupies bits inside a register.

Spatial editing means insert, move, resize, and delete operations must keep those ranges valid.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text: Each level has its own unit. A register offset is measured in bytes; a field offset is measured in bits. Do not reuse calculations between levels without converting units explicitly.

docs.title: Saved positions are authoritative
docs.text:
Array order controls presentation, but offsets and bit ranges control hardware. Valid maps may contain empty space, so positions cannot be reconstructed from array order alone.

Register bits: 31                          0
               [ STATUS ][ gap ][ ENABLE ]

The gap is intentional data, not an error.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operation Expected result Insert Add an item in available space and return its final position Delete Remove an item and apply the layout rule for that editor Move Change order while preserving unrelated space where required Resize Change one range without crossing a neighbor or boundary

The exact layout rule depends on the operation. Bit-field insertion and deletion close gaps; field movement keeps existing gaps. This distinction is deliberate.

docs.title: One-operation pipeline
docs.text: The editor must not save an intermediate overlapping layout. One gesture creates one complete document update so undo and document versions remain predictable.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
After a successful operation:

  • every item stays inside its parent range;
  • sibling items do not overlap;
  • saved positions match the visual layout;
  • array order matches the editor's display order;
  • selection follows the moved item rather than its old index;
  • editor-only row IDs are not written to YAML.

An operation that cannot meet these guarantees should return a clear error and leave the document unchanged.

docs.title: Main implementation areas
docs.text:
Area Responsibility LayoutEngine.ts Bit-field position rules SpatialInsertionService.ts Insert fields, registers, and blocks FieldOperationService.ts Structured field operations reorderPreview.ts Shared drag destination calculation rowIdentity.ts Preserve selection across reparsing

See bit field handling for detailed field rules and bit field developer reference for functions and callbacks.

docs.title: Vivado Interface Catalog
docs.text: IPCraft can read interface definitions from an installed Vivado catalog. This lets users choose interfaces that Vivado already understands instead of recreating each one as a custom interface.

docs.title: Interface choices
docs.text:
IPCraft works with three kinds of interface:

Kind Source Best use Built-in Shipped with IPCraft Common buses supported directly by the generator Vivado catalog Read from the local Vivado installation Vendor interfaces that Vivado already defines Custom Defined in the project Project-specific signal groups

The source affects how an interface is discovered, but the canvas presents all three as interfaces with named logical signals.

docs.title: Discovery flow
docs.text: IPCraft reads the same interface metadata that Vivado uses for IP packaging. The source files remain owned by Vivado; IPCraft stores only the selected interface identity and the user's signal mapping.

docs.title: Mapping signals
docs.text:
Adding a catalog interface does not discard existing ports. IPCraft opens a mapping step where each logical interface signal can be connected to an existing IP port or a newly created port.

For example, a logical clock signal may map to the IP port sample_clk even if the catalog calls that signal CLK.

The saved mapping is explicit. Later generation does not need to guess from port names.

docs.title: What is saved
docs.text:
The IP core document records:

  • the interface identity supplied by Vivado;
  • the interface mode, when the definition supports modes;
  • the mapping from logical signals to physical IP ports.

It does not copy the complete Vivado installation catalog into the project. Another machine must have a compatible definition when it needs to browse or validate that interface.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Catalog discovery depends on a configured Vivado installation.
  • A catalog entry does not automatically provide IPCraft HDL generation rules.
  • A user must review signal direction, width, and clock or reset relationships.
  • Project-specific interfaces should still use a reusable custom definition.

docs.title: Implementation map
docs.text:
Responsibility Location Read Vivado interface files Extension-side Vivado services Present search and selection IP Core webview Save interface mapping IP core domain and YAML editing layers Generate Vivado metadata src/generator/

See Custom interfaces when the interface is not available from the built-in or Vivado catalogs.

docs.title: Developer Changelog
docs.text:
The technical record of changes to IPCraft, for contributors and maintainers. It names the modules, commands, schema keys, template-context contract versions, issues and pull requests behind each change, and includes internal work (refactors, CI, packaging, tests) that does not affect users.

User-facing release notes are in CHANGELOG.md at the repository root. That file ships in the VSIX and is shown on the Marketplace, so it describes each release in user terms only. When you make a change, record it here; if users will notice it, also add a plain-language entry to the release notes.

docs.text:
• System design diff: ghosts in exported images and ipcraft diff --image (phase 2). SystemLevelRequest gains union?: UnionAdditions; drawSystemLevel lays the level out with withUnion(graph, union) (isolation, buildElkInput and toFlowElements(..., ghosts) take the union graph; analyzeClocks, clockDecor and changeDecor keep the open design, as in the viewer), and the caller builds changes with buildChangeMarks(diff, graph, withUnion(graph, union).ghosts) so the marks carry the ghosts.   • System design diff: ghosts for what was removed, the Show removed toggle and the union layout in the viewer (phase 2). New pure services/systemDiagram/diff/unionAdditions.ts: unionAdditions(base, current, diff): UnionAdditions (the type is in src/domain/systemGraphDiff.ts: instances, pins, boundaryPins, nets, JSON-serializable) is computed on the base after the diff's renames (findingsBase) and moves (relocateInstances) are applied, so renamed and moved blocks are never ghosts. instances: the removed blocks whose level exists in current, only the topmost of a removed subtree; boundaryPins: the removed external ports of / (a removed hierarchy pin has no node on the level it belongs to, so it is not one); nets: for each base net on a level current has (clock and reset nets left out), its pins that exist in the union are grouped by what current still connects (buildPeerLookup of current, union-find), and a net with two or more groups becomes one ghost net ghost:<base net id> with the first pin of each group, so a lost connection is drawn once and a kept one is not repeated; pins: the pins of those nets that a block of current lost (the interconnect port of a removed slave), which the spec's three-field shape could not give a wire an end for. Webview: layout/unionGraph.ts (withUnion(graph, union) merges the additions into a copy of the graph and returns the Ghosts sets of ids: instances, pins by block, boundary node ids, nets; layoutNetsByEndpoint keeps a ghost net off the pins of the open design; withoutGhosts(layout, ghosts); openCellCount). useCompareToggles (Marks and Removed, each on again when the base changes, Version only) is split from useCompareView(graph, toggles, levelPath, isolate, ghosts) because whether ghosts are shown (ghostsShown = marksOn && removedOn && hasRemoved) decides which graph the navigation, isolation, search, Outline and Details use (useUnionGraph: viewGraph is the union while ghosts are shown, else the open design); the layout (useElkLayout(layoutGraph, ..., ghosts, ghostsShown)) is always made from the union while a comparison has ghosts and leaves the ghosts out of the returned layout when they are hidden (the ghosts the layout was made with are kept with it), so no toggle moves a block; the analyses (unconnectedPins, analyzeClocks), the findings and the exports keep reading the open design. toFlowElements takes the Ghosts (default none, so the image renderer and ipcraft diff --image are unchanged): PinRow.ghost, the net lookup, frameData (inner, ghostPins, cells). Marks: MarkStatus and PinMarkKind gain removed; buildChangeMarks(diff, graph, ghosts) marks the shown ghosts (blocks, ports, a removed pin mark, removedNets) so the canvas, the Outline, the minimap, the legend (removed kind, removedWire) and Details (GhostDetails.tsx: type and parameters from the base, no source line, definition or level) read one carrier; ElkEdgeData.changeRemoved draws a ghost wire dashed in --sd-change-removed; a ghost block is dashed with the name struck through (CSS on data-change='removed'), a ghost hierarchy has no expand toggle and is not entered, and a ghost pin row keeps its height but is empty while its ghost is hidden. The isolation is worked out on the union graph (useIsolation(layoutGraph, nav, ghosts, ghostsShown); its openNodeCount and levelNodeCount leave ghosts out) so a toggle never changes the isolated layout; useDiagramNavigation(graph, ghosts) refuses to enter or expand a ghost; InstanceDetails and BoundaryDetails take unconnected status from openNetsByEndpoint (the open design) and list a lost wire apart; the flow-node building moved from elkLayout.ts to layout/flowNodes.ts.   • System design diff: workspace definitions read from the base revision in the viewer (phase 4). New pure enrichment/revisionIo.ts: revisionIo(io, readAt) wraps an EnrichmentIo<R> so definition files are read as they were at a revision (ReadAt<R> = (ref) => Promise<string | undefined>, undefined when the file is not there). listIpFiles takes the working-tree entries, runs matchDefinitions on them for the graph the pipeline is about to match, re-reads only the matched files with readAt and rebuilds them with ipEntryFromText (same location); at most 8 are read at once; a matched file that is absent or does not parse at the revision, and every unmatched entry, is dropped (a VLNV that differs at the revision is read and then not matched by the pipeline). Matching uses the working tree's index, so a definition that only exists at the revision or whose VLNV or name changed since is not found. listHdlFiles and listQsysFiles are the working-tree lists; readText reads at the revision and throws the new FileAbsentError (enrichmentIo.ts) for an absent file, which enrichSystemGraph (skips the HDL file) and expandSubsystems (the instance stays opaque) skip without log line or diagnostic, skips an HDL file over HDL_MAX_BYTES at the revision like the index, and wraps a failing readAt in the new SourceFailedError, which both rethrow, so a git failure is never mistaken for a missing definition (the list of .ip.yml files rejects too). The module doc lists the limits: matching uses the working tree's index, and an HDL file's ports are read from the text at the revision for the unit the working-tree entry names. EnrichmentIo.listIpFiles therefore gains the parameters (graph, designFile), which enrichSystemGraph passes after expandSubsystems (so instances grafted from a subsystem match too); the CLI io and the VS Code index ignore them. SystemDesignEnricher.enrich(read, designFile, readAt?) uses revisionIo(this.io, readAt) with readAt (the untrusted-workspace early return is unchanged). gitRevisions.resolveCommit(repo, ref) (getCommit of <ref>^{commit}, which peels an annotated tag so a hash quoted in its message is not picked up) gives the hash a ref names when the base is picked, and pickCompareBase reads the design and every definition at that hash, so a branch or HEAD that moves later does not mix revisions (a label that is the ref itself, such as HEAD or a branch, gets the short hash appended, for example HEAD (1a2b3c4); commit and merge-base labels already carry theirs). revisionFileReader(repo, hash) reads one file at the hash: show, then getObjectDetails/UnknownPath tells an absent file (undefined) from a failure (rejects with git's reason); an absent file is looked up in one diffWith(hash) per comparison (INDEX_RENAMED: working-tree path to old path) and read under its old path, so a moved definition file is found; each file is read once and a failed read is retried on the next call. CompareBase.readDefinitionAt is that reader (not for a file, an open tab or a missing base). A rejection reaches diffEnriched, which falls back to both sides as read (the existing fallback) and logs it once per diff. SystemDesignCompare<R> (generic in the reader's argument, so it stays free of vscode) keeps it in BaseOrigin.readDefinitionAt and diffEnriched passes it to enrich; the enriched-base cache key is unchanged. CompareResult and DiagramCompare gain baseDefinitions: BaseDefinitions ('revision' | 'workspace' | 'none'; none when the comparison fell back to both sides as read, and PanelCompare.describe sets it in an untrusted workspace); FindingsTable (definitionsNote) says The base is checked with the definitions at <short label>; the current side with those of this workspace. for revision (a commit label is shortened to its hash), Both sides are checked with the definitions of this workspace. for workspace, The base did not exist: every finding of the file is new. for a missing base, and that definitions are not read for none. ipcraft diff is unchanged (no workspace enrichment). Tests: revisionIo.test.ts, SystemDesignEnricher.test.ts, SystemDesignCompare.test.ts (a definition that differs between the revision and the workspace shows as a new pin and finding), gitRevisions.test.ts (resolveCommit, readFileAt, revisionFileReader), pickCompareBase.test.ts, SystemDiagramProvider.test.ts, FindingsTable.test.tsx, compareSystemDesign.test.ts (e2e, real git extension). (#302)

  • System design diff: a file that was renamed, or did not exist, at the base revision (phase 4). New pure emptySystemGraph(name, format) in src/domain/emptySystemGraph.ts (one root level /, nothing else). SystemGraphDiffSide gains path? (the base was read under another path) and missing?: true (the file did not exist there), set by the caller on diff.base after diffSystemGraphs; the new pure baseNote(base, label, quote?) in diff/baseNote.ts writes the one sentence (The file did not exist at <ref>: everything is added. or Read at <ref> as <old path> (renamed since).) for diffToMarkdown (a code span for the path), after the Comparing line, and for the Changes bar of ChangesTable.tsx (plain), so reports without either field are byte-identical.   • GitHub Action for the system design diff (phase 4). New composite action actions/system-design-diff/ (action.yml, comment.js with comment.d.ts): for each design in designs it runs node "$CLI" diff <design> --base <base> [--head] --out <report dir>/<n>.md [--ignore-version-only] [--fail-on], records the exit code (<n>.exit) and stderr (<n>.err) without stopping at a failure (GitHub's shell: bash runs with -e, hence if ...; then code=0; else code=$?; fi), writes every report to the job summary, upserts one pull request comment marked <!-- ipcraft-system-design-diff --> (paginated GET, PATCH or POST through the REST API with fetch, 65536-character limit, surrogate-safe truncation, the last stderr lines for a run without a report), and fails the job afterwards when a run failed. The required cli input is a dist/cli.js built in the same job from a pinned ipcraft-vscode checkout: the standalone npm package is not published, so the action fetches nothing by package name. Inputs reach the shell only through env; the comment is posted on pull_request events only (fork pull requests get the job summary; the docs warn against pull_request_target); an empty base or a missing cli stops early with an ::error::. Tests: systemDesignDiffComment.test.ts, systemDesignDiffAction.test.ts (runs the step under bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail with a stub CLI). (#302)

  • System design diff: moved blocks (phase 4, rename and move pairing). InstanceChange.status gains moved (with basePath, level the new parent, parameters empty and pins the connection changes of the block) and DiffSummary gains moved (always present, 0 when there is none, so the JSON of every report has the key). renameInstances is generalized to relocateInstances(graph, relocations) in the new relocate.ts (a map from path to new path; a renamed block keeps its parent level, a moved one gets parentLevel(to) as parent and leaves the child list of its old level for the one of its new level, when that level exists in the graph; nets stay on their levels, endpoints, level ids of moved hierarchies and the segment texts follow the path); findingsBase keeps applying only the renames, because unconnectedPins is per level and a moved block's nets stay on their old level in the moved base. New moves.ts findMoves(base, current, plain, renamed), run by diffSystemGraphs on the base findRenames returns (it now returns it with the diff) and the diff of that base: candidates are a removed and an added block with the same last name, kind, type string, parameters and pin names (signature is exported from renames.ts with a place prefix: the parent for renames, the name for moves) and a different parent, each the topmost of its subtree (its parent is not itself removed, or added), the only pair of its signature; all pairs are applied at once and diffed once; a pair is dropped when anything differs strictly below the moved block or the block has a change other than pins (no parameter, type or attribute change), and the rest starts again from the original base. If the moved diff touches a block that was paired as a rename (renames run first, without the moves), the moves with a pin among the peers, in either graph, of that renamed block (or of anything below it) are dropped, the others stay; when none can be told, all are dropped (movesNextTo). The accepted moves' own entries leave the diff (summary.changed follows) and come back as moved entries carrying their pins; the base names for labels merge the renamed and the moved paths. basePeerLabels (pinPeers.ts) writes the base peers of a pin relative to the level the pin had in the base (parentLevel(baseName(owner))), so a block that moved with its neighbour is not written absolute; peerLabel is unchanged. changeCount counts moved, so --fail-on changes does. Report: CHANGE_SIGNS.moved is » (U+00BB; neither ↳ nor → is in the embedded Plex fonts, so renamed images already draw → in a fallback font, while » is in them; it is added to scripts/generate-font-metrics.js and fontMetrics.generated.ts), one row per move (old path under Base, new path under Current, then pin rows as for a changed block), · »N moved in the summary only when N > 0; the goldens without a move are unchanged. Viewer: a sixth kind in CHANGE_KINDS (offered and counted only when summary.moved > 0), MarkStatus moved with the renamed color (--sd-change-renamed, palette.change.moved, the minimap, the legend and the image marks follow), title Moved from <old parent path>, the pins of a moved block are marked, an address change promotes it to changed (Changed: moved from /, address changed), and segmentOwners maps the base spelling of a moved block's segments to it. Not paired, on purpose: a block moved and renamed at once, a block moved into a hierarchy that is new (its parent is an added block), a block with a changed parameter, type or pin list. The test does not pair a block moved into another level under the same name as a rename of renames.test.ts now expects a move for a block that changed levels under the same name. Tests: moves.test.ts (with the reference check moveReference.ts, built on the one-at-a-time oracle renameReference.ts, which now also moves), renames.test.ts, diffReport.test.ts and changeRows.test.ts (golden zynq_gpio_move.expected.md, pair zynq_gpio_base.bd / zynq_gpio_move_current.bd), diff.node.test.ts, changeSummary.test.ts, changeMarks.test.ts, changeTargets.test.ts, CompareControl.test.tsx, ChangesTable.test.tsx, DiagramCanvasChanges.test.tsx, legend.test.ts, minimap.test.ts, palette.test.ts, systemLevelSvg.test.ts. (#302)

  • System design diff: Version only toggle in the viewer (phase 2). useCompareView owns versionOnly (default true; a preference of the panel, so unlike Marks it is not reset when the base changes) and derives one memoized shown: DiagramCompare | undefined: the incoming comparison itself when versionOnly is true or its summary.version is 0, else the comparison with withoutVersionOnly(diff). marks, rows, changes, details and markedIds all read shown; the hook also returns versionOnly, setVersionOnly and hasVersionOnly (the incoming summary.version > 0). WorkbenchLayout passes shown to the toolbar's CompareControl and to BottomPanel (changes.compare), so the counts, the Changes tab and its chips follow the filter; useBottomTab keeps the incoming baseLabel. CompareControlProps gains versionOnly?: { on, onChange }, a pressed-state button (aria-label="Show version-only changes", the v sign, so it is not confused with the Changes tab chip Version only) rendered next to Marks only when given. Export: SystemExportView gains ignoreVersionOnly?: boolean (parsed boolean-only), SystemExportState the same flag, and buildSystemExportView sends it only with marks, and WorkbenchLayout sets it only when the comparison has version-only changes and the toggle is off; ImageExportHost.exportSystem applies withoutVersionOnly(diff) before buildChangeMarks when it is set. shownKinds(summary, { version }) (default true) leaves the version kind out while the toggle is off, because summary.version === 0 after filtering cannot be told from a diff without version-only blocks: CompareControl (showVersion) and ChangesTable (showVersion, through BottomPanel's changes.showVersion) get the toggle state, so the toolbar count and the chip are not listed, as in the ipcraft diff --ignore-version-only summary; ChangesTable resets the version chip to shown when the kind comes back. A version-only block that also has an address change is still marked changed through the segment path. Tests: useCompareView.test.tsx, CompareControl.test.tsx, changeSummary.test.ts, ChangesTable.test.tsx, SystemDiagramApp.test.tsx, exportView.test.ts, imageExport.test.ts, ImageExportHost.test.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: marks in the viewer's exported images (phase 2). SystemExportView gains marks?: boolean (the comparison marks are drawn on the canvas); parseSystemExportView keeps a boolean and drops any other value. Webview: SystemExportState gains marksOn (from useCompareView().marksOn, passed by WorkbenchLayout to useDiagramExport), and buildSystemExportView adds marks: true only while it is set, so an export without a comparison sends the same message as before. SystemDiagramProvider keeps the CompareResult of the last published graph next to lastGraph (set in publish, undefined when the graph is published without a comparison) and passes its diff to ImageExportHost.exportSystem(document, graph, message, diff?), which sets changes: buildChangeMarks(diff, graph) in the SystemLevelRequest when view.marks is true and a diff is given (buildChangeMarks is imported on first use); otherwise the request has no changes and is unchanged. A marks: true view without a diff (the comparison ended before the message arrived) exports without marks, with no error. Not yet: ghosts for removed blocks, ports and wires, the union layout. Tests: ImageExportHost.test.ts, imageExport.test.ts, exportView.test.ts, useDiagramExport.test.tsx, SystemDiagramApp.test.tsx, SystemDiagramProvider.test.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: change marks in exported images and ipcraft diff --image (phase 2 and 3). palette.ts gains Palette.change (added, changed, renamed, version, newWire), pinned per theme to the docs-screenshot token values; scripts/docs-screenshots/theme/light.css and dark.css gain the four --vscode-gitDecoration-*ResourceForeground tokens, with the values of the bundled git extension (light #587c0c, #895503, #8e8e90, deleted #ad0707; dark #81b88b, #e2c08d, #8c8c8c, deleted #c74e39), which are not in the core color registry, and renamed is --vscode-charts-purple. renderSystemLevelSvg takes an optional changes?: ChangeDecor (type import only) and merges it into the node data (change) and wire data (changeNew) as the canvas does, so output without it is byte-identical. New shared/render/changeSvg.ts (status border and dotted version-only border, header sign and ~ N inside items, port sign, marked pin label color); blockSvg.ts and pinSvg.ts use it (the selection outline wins over a change border, which wins over a crossing border; a crossing pin label wins over a change color, as in the CSS), decorSvg.ts selectionRing takes an optional color, legendSvg.ts draws the kind swatches with sign, New wire and - N removed (layoutLegend takes the ChangeLegend), and edgeSvg follows markedStroke of ElkEdge.tsx. SystemLevelRequest.changes?: ChangeMarks; drawSystemLevel runs changeDecor on the laid-out flow after the clock decor. diffArgv.ts parses --image <file> into CliDiffArgs.image (extension checked with renderOutputFormat, else Unsupported image file '<f>': the extension must be .svg, .png, .jpg or .jpeg); new cli/diffImage.ts writeDiffImage draws level / of the current graph with buildChangeMarks and the RENDER_DEFAULTS that ipcraft render now shares (renderArgv.ts); runCliDiff(args, roots?) writes it after the report, and index.ts resolves the resource roots (loadResourceRoots) only for --image and prints Wrote <file> to standard output, or to standard error when the report is on standard output. With --ignore-version-only the marks leave out version-only blocks, as the report does. Tests: systemLevelSvg.test.ts, palette.test.ts, renderService.node.test.ts, diff.node.test.ts, argv.test.ts.
  • System design diff: segment marks in the Address map tab (phase 3, fourth slice). New pure src/webview/systemDiagram/addressMapRows.ts: addressMapRows(graph, diff?) returns AddressMapRow { segment: SegmentFields, format, change?, changedFields?, baseShown? }. Without a diff it is the current segments as they were; with one, each current row carries its added or changed SegmentChange (matched by the exact key addressSpace + '\u0000' + segment, as diffSegments does) and the removed ones follow, built from the change with the base's offset and range and diff.base.format. SegmentFields is the narrow Pick of AddressSegment the table reads plus an optional line (a removed segment has none); segmentHigh, segmentRangeText, segmentLevel and segmentTexts accept the Pick of the fields they read, and segmentTexts takes an optional format. AddressMapTable takes diff? (from BottomPanel) and, with it, adds a sign column (sd-sign / data-sign), marks changed value cells (td[data-changed], --sd-change-changed) with a Base: title, and dims removed rows (Not in this revision, not clickable, Source -). Without a diff the DOM is unchanged. No protocol or engine change. (#302)
  • System design diff: ipcraft diff --fail-on (phase 3, third slice). diffArgv.ts parses --fail-on changes|new-findings into CliDiffArgs.failOn (another value: Invalid --fail-on '<v>': expected 'changes' or 'new-findings'). New pure failOnReason(diff, findings, failOn, ignoreVersionOnly) in cli/diff.ts: changes fails on a summary total above 0 (the new changeCount(summary) in ignoreVersionOnly.ts, also used by the No changes. check of diffReport.ts: added + removed + changed + renamed + version, after withoutVersionOnly when --ignore-version-only), new-findings on findings.new.length > 0; the reason includes the option (3 changes (--fail-on changes), 1 new finding (--fail-on new-findings)); finding differences alone are not changes and resolved findings never fail. runCliDiff sets CliDiffResult.failed (the reason) after the report is produced, so the report is returned or written as before; main then prints Diff check failed: <reason> (--fail-on <value>) with console.error and returns 1 (errors stay Diff failed: ..., also 1). The Markdown and JSON reports are unchanged. Tests: argv.test.ts, diff.node.test.ts (failOnReason and main on the zynq pair, the reversed pair and a file against itself). (#302)
  • System design diff: Findings tab in the system viewer (phase 3, second slice). diffFindings.ts is split into the exported steps findingsOf(graph) (key -> finding), findingsBase(base, diff) (the base with the renames of the diff applied; the same object when there are none) and compareFindings(baseFindings, currentFindings); diffFindings composes them and its output is unchanged except that CrossingFinding gains fromInstance and toInstance (the CrossingEnd.instance of each end, null for an external port or an unknown reset source), so the viewer can select a crossing. The JSON of ipcraft diff therefore has these two fields on every crossing finding; the Markdown report does not use them and is byte-identical. New pure diff/findingRows.ts (findingRows(findings) -> FindingRow { sign, finding, kind, where, detail } with the Cell model of changeRows.ts): the one row model of the Markdown Findings table (diffReport.ts renders it with its existing render and table) and of the viewer. SystemDesignCompare memoizes findingsOf per graph object (a private WeakMap), so the cached enriched base is analysed once per comparison and only the current side on each edit (a base with renamed blocks is a fresh copy for each diff, so it is analysed each time); CompareResult and DiagramCompare gain findings (additive; both stages, read against read and enriched against enriched, carry it). Webview: BottomTab gains findings (right after changes, only while comparing, count = new + resolved), FindingsTable.tsx (sign, Finding, Where, Detail; a note that both revisions use the same workspace definitions; New and Resolved chips; the row selects its target through the new pure findingTarget(graph, finding) in changeTargets.ts, which also gets isTargetSelected and NOT_IN_REVISION, moved out of ChangesTable.tsx so both tables share them; a crossing selects its sink block, else its source block, else the external port it ends at, else the one it starts at; the new TargetRow.tsx is the clickable row, with the select dispatch, of both tables), comparedFindingTexts in panelFilter.ts, the .sd-sign[data-finding] colors and wrapping in systemDiagram.css, and useBottomTab falls back to the Address map for both comparison tabs when the comparison ends (the Findings tab never opens by itself). Not in this slice: findings on the diagram, a count of findings in the compare toolbar. Tests: diffFindings.test.ts, findingRows.test.ts, diffReport.test.ts (goldens unchanged), SystemDesignCompare.test.ts, changeTargets.test.ts, FindingsTable.test.tsx, BottomPanelChanges.test.tsx, panelFilter.test.ts, SystemDiagramProvider.test.ts, system-diagram-compare.spec.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: findings diff in the engine and ipcraft diff (phase 3, first slice). New hand-written types in src/domain/systemGraphDiff.ts: FindingsDiff { new, resolved } and Finding = UnconnectedFinding | CrossingFinding (JSON-serializable, sorted by kind, level, label). New pure src/services/systemDiagram/diff/diffFindings.ts (diffFindings(base, current, diff)): the findings of a graph are every unconnectedPins entry and every analyzeClocks crossing of kind data or reset with status cross (block crossings, related, inside, unchecked and ok are not findings); each analysis runs once per graph. Identity is the pin (cls|level|nodeId|pin) or the two crossing ends (kind|endKey(from)>endKey(to), unknown for a reset source that is not known), never crossing.id, which holds the net id of an unknown reset source and Vivado renames nets. The base is analysed after renameInstances with the renames of the diff, so a renamed block's findings are neither new nor resolved and resolved findings carry the new names. DiffReportOptions gains findings?; diffToMarkdown writes a ### Findings table (New rows, then Resolved, with the no-definitions note) after the summary line, appends N new findings · M resolved findings to the summary and no longer prints No changes. when only findings differ; with no findings given or none different, the report is unchanged. cli/diff.ts computes the findings once; the JSON report is the diff plus a findings field (always present; --ignore-version-only does not filter it). The golden zynq_gpio.expected.md gains the row Resolved | undriven pin | led_o (the removed external port was unconnected in the base); the golden tests of diffReport.test.ts now pass the findings of the pair. Not in this slice: the viewer Findings tab, a count of findings in the viewer's compare bar. Tests: diffFindings.test.ts (new, resolved, unchanged, renamed block, a reset crossing whose net is renamed, sort order by kind, level and label, no difference of any diff fixture with itself), diffReport.test.ts, diff.node.test.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: renamed blocks. InstanceChange.status gains renamed (with basePath; parameters and pins empty) and DiffSummary gains renamed. The old diffSystemGraphs body is now diffWithoutRenames.ts (also the home of summarize); diffSystemGraphs runs it, calls findRenames in renames.ts, which returns the renames and the diff of the accepted round (the plain diff when there are none), and merges the renamed entries into it by path. renames.ts also has the pure renameInstance(graph, from, to) (instance and level keys, paths, names, child lists, net endpoints and the level and id of the nets of a renamed level, address segment instances and the leading path of the addressSpace and segment texts; the input is not mutated). Pairing is conservative: a removed and an added block of one parent level that exists on both sides, with the same kind, type string, parameters and pin names, alone in their signature; the pair is accepted only if the diff of the renamed base has no instance change at or below the added path, all candidate pairs are applied to the base at once, the diff is taken once, pairs with a change at or below their added path are dropped and the rest starts again from the original base until none is dropped (order-free; the Base side of pin changes writes renamed blocks by their base paths through PeerLookup.baseName, set by createPinContext from the optional renamed argument of diffWithoutRenames). Detection never hides a change. It can show a connection change that the diff without it attributed to the removed and the added block. A block that only lost or gained a neighbour may no longer be listed; the change then shows on that neighbour. instanceType is exported from diffInstances.ts. changeRows.ts: ChangeSign gains →, CellPart.mark, one row per rename; the marked characters come from the new pure nameDifference.ts (common prefix and suffix unmarked, the middle marked); diffReport.ts writes a marked part as a bold code span, merges adjacent unmarked code parts into one span and adds · →N renamed to the summary line only when N > 0 (the existing goldens are unchanged). Viewer: a fifth kind in CHANGE_KINDS (chip, badge, toolbar count), .sd-mark and the → colour in systemDiagram.css. The segment texts follow the renamed owner in every format (.bd, write_bd_tcl, .qsys, qsys-script): the leading part of the addressSpace or segment text that spells its master or slave instance (path without the leading slash) and is followed by / (Vivado, with an optional leading / kept, and the subsystem/ prefix of a grafted subsystem) or . (Platform Designer and qsys-script) is replaced, derived from masterInstance / slaveInstance, so uart never touches uart_0. Not covered: moves to another level, renamed-and-changed blocks. The Renamed chip and the toolbar count appear only when a block was renamed. Fixture pair nios_rename_*.qsys. Tests: renames.test.ts (with the reference check renameReference.ts: the detected diff must equal the plain diff of the base with exactly the accepted renames applied, plus the renamed entries), nameDifference.test.ts, the fixture pair zynq_gpio_rename_*.bd with its golden report, changeRows.test.ts, diffReport.test.ts, diff.node.test.ts, diffSystemGraphs.realFiles.test.ts, ChangesTable.test.tsx, CompareControl.test.tsx, changeSummary.test.ts, panelFilter.test.ts, system-diagram-compare.spec.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: compare in the system viewer (phase 1, second slice). New pure diff/changeRows.ts (changeRows(diff, { ignoreVersionOnly }) → flat ChangeRow[]: sign, section, level, target, and the cells subject, change, base, current, each a structured Cell = items of CellPart { text, code? }, so names and values stay one piece whatever they contain; cellText(cell) gives the plain text; target is an instance path, an external port, or a segment by address space and name that the webview resolves to its slave block with changeTargets.ts); diffReport.ts renders its Markdown tables from those rows by wrapping code parts in code spans and escaping | (the golden files are unchanged; no cell text is parsed anywhere). Extension host: services/systemDiagram/compare/gitRevisions.ts (a hand-typed view of the vscode.git API: openRepository, listRevisions, readRevision; no child_process) and SystemDesignCompare.ts (the base graph of one panel, kept as read; diffRead compares it with the early graph, diffEnriched enriches the base anew with the same enricher and document path as the current side and compares the enriched graphs, so both sides always have the same definitions); providers/systemDiagram/pickCompareBase.ts (quick pick, input box, open dialog). SystemDiagramProvider attaches compare to every published graph message, handles the new startCompare and stopCompare messages, tracks its panels and exposes compareActive() for the new command fpga-ip-core.compareSystemDesign (commands/compareSystemDesign.ts). Webview: messageState keeps compare; CompareControl.tsx (toolbar), ChangesTable.tsx and a fifth changes tab in BottomPanel (first, only during a comparison), changeSummary.ts, changeTargets.ts, changeTexts in panelFilter.ts, hooks/useBottomTab.ts (opens the tab when a comparison starts, falls back to the Address map when it ends). __mocks__/vscode.ts gained window.showInputBox and extensions.getExtension. Direction and bases: DiagramCompare also carries currentLabel and canSwap, ChangesTable shows one sticky bar Base … → Current … (short labels from compareLabels.ts, full ones in titles; Swap; summary; chips whose titles say what each kind means), renders an address row as space → segment with added/removed/address changed (the shared ChangeRow and the Markdown report are unchanged), and a Swap button posts swapCompare (through useSystemDiagramMessages, DiagramWorkbench, WorkbenchLayout and BottomPanel as onSwapCompare). pickCompareBase offers the open design tabs (openDesignTabs.ts, text of the tab) and listFileCommits (repository.log({ path, maxEntries: 20 }), none when log throws) besides the revisions, grouped under separators (RevisionChoice.group); a picked file has CompareBase.file. providers/systemDiagram/PanelCompare.ts is the per-panel comparison controller: it keeps the base file (canSwap is true when it is set, so SystemDesignCompare stays free of vscode) and the swap request that waits for its panel, and starts, stops and swaps the comparison; a file base is read in its own format, a revision in the document's. providers/systemDiagram/DiagramPanels.ts tracks the open panels (by document URI, a visible one first) and the pending swap requests. Swap reveals an open panel of the base (openWith would open a second editor in another group) and otherwise queues a request and calls vscode.openWith; the new panel takes the request when it registers and keeps it until ready, and a request is dropped when that panel closes first, when the requesting panel is disposed, or, when openWith resolves without a panel having taken it, after a 5 second grace period (at once when openWith rejects). Not in this slice: marks on the canvas, the findings diff, choosing a revision for the current side, rename pairing. Tests: changeRows.test.ts, gitRevisions.test.ts, SystemDesignCompare.test.ts, pickCompareBase.test.ts, SystemDiagramProvider.test.ts, DiagramPanels.test.ts, ChangesTable.test.tsx, compareLabels.test.ts, CompareControl.test.tsx, BottomPanelChanges.test.tsx, SystemDiagramApp.test.tsx, system-diagram-compare.spec.ts (browser), and src/test/e2e/suite/compareSystemDesign.test.ts, which runs the git adapter, the open-tab list, the quick pick and the command against a real VS Code. The fpga-ip-core.compareSystemDesign command returns whether a system diagram was active. Marks on the diagram (phase 2, first slice): PinChange gains gained and lost (peers by identity, decided in diffPins.ts, so a renamed block is neither; the goldens and renameReference.ts are unchanged). Webview: the pure changeMarks.ts (buildChangeMarks, isNewWire, wireEndLabel over the engine's peerLabel, markedNodeIds) and changeDecor.ts (the per-node NodeChange, the new wire ids and the legend, computed once per layout and comparison and merged by useCanvasElements.ts into node data.change and edge data.changeNew), ChangeBadges.tsx, ChangeCell.tsx (the cell renderer, extracted from ChangesTable.tsx), InstanceChanges.tsx (the Changes section of Details), hooks/useCompareView.ts (Marks toggle, restarts on when the base label changes; Changes only through useIsolation.isolate), the --sd-change-* custom properties in systemDiagram.css (one definition for the Changes tab and the diagram), the new-wire stroke in ElkEdge.tsx, signs in the outline, the minimap colors and the legend entries. Not yet: ghosts for removed blocks, ports and wires, the union layout, marks in exported images and ipcraft render, the findings diff, the Address map diff. Tests: changeMarks.test.ts, changeDecor.test.ts, DiagramCanvasChanges.test.tsx, ChangeMarksPanels.test.tsx, useCompareView.test.tsx, CompareControl.test.tsx, ElkEdge.test.tsx, minimap.test.ts, legend.test.ts, DiagramLegend.test.tsx, SystemDiagramApp.test.tsx, diffSystemGraphs.test.ts, renames.test.ts, system-diagram-compare.spec.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: engine and ipcraft diff (phase 1, first slice). New hand-written types src/domain/systemGraphDiff.ts (SystemGraphDiff: InstanceChange, PortChange, SegmentChange, ValueChange, summary; JSON-serializable). The pure diffSystemGraphs(base, current) in src/services/systemDiagram/diff/ compares two SystemGraphs by identity (instance path, pin owner and name, external port name, address space plus segment, parameter key); connections are compared per pin through its peers, the other endpoints of every net, on any level, that holds the pin (pinPeers.ts: an instance pin is its absolute path and name, a boundary pin its level and name), never by net name or id, and order and line fields are not read. Instances are added, removed, changed or version (only the fourth VLNV field, or the Platform Designer module version, differs); pins are compared by peers (the other endpoints of every net, on any level, that holds the pin; a peer is written relative to the level of the reported pin and absolute otherwise) and, for the pins of a hier instance that exists on both sides, also by attributes (pinAttributes.ts; the direction only when both sides declare it, not when it was inferred; direction, signalType, vlnv, interfaceType, width, then parameters; PinChange.attributes); a hierarchy has two views of each pin, the outside one on the nets of the parent level and the inside one on the nets of the hierarchy's own level, and both are classified (the inside view is a PinChange with inside: true, listed after the outside one; peers of a boundary pin of another level are written /level/path:pin) and only the pin that moved is reported (diffPins.ts: peers that are pins of added or removed blocks are explained away, and a pin that kept more connections than every pin it gained or lost is a host and is not reported; a classified pin (a pin of an instance of either graph, an external port, or the inside view of a hierarchy pin) is reported by some caller, so two pins on opposite sides of a change are never both suppressed, and an endpoint that is none of these (such as a pin of a block in neither graph) never suppresses; added and removed instances list their connected pins), external ports by the same attributes and their parameters; segments by offset and range, case-insensitively. Split into diffInstances.ts, diffPins.ts, diffPorts.ts, diffSegments.ts, valueChanges.ts, pinAttributes.ts, compareText.ts, ignoreVersionOnly.ts. diffReport.ts (diffToMarkdown) writes the stable Markdown report. The new command ipcraft diff (cli/diff.ts, cli/diffArgv.ts) compares a file against a git revision (--base, --head) or two files, with --format markdown|json, --out and --ignore-version-only; cli/gitFile.ts (readGitFile) reads a revision with git rev-parse --show-prefix and git show <ref>:<path> through execFile (no shell, a ref starting with - is rejected). Not in this slice: viewer, findings diff, rename pairing, image output, --fail-on, workspace enrichment, git rename detection. Tests: diffSystemGraphs.test.ts, diffReport.test.ts (golden reports of the fixture pairs in src/test/fixtures/system-design/diff/), diffSystemGraphs.realFiles.test.ts (set IPCRAFT_BD_SAMPLES), argv.test.ts, diff.node.test.ts (including a temporary git repository). (#302, concept)
  • System viewer: JSON .bd reader. New pure BdJsonReader.ts (readBdJson(text, fileName)) turns the design object of a Vivado 2018.3+ .bd file into the same SystemGraph as readBdTcl, with source.format 'vivado-bd'. It writes into SystemGraphBuilder (new format constructor parameter and addInstancePin), then runs inferPinDirections and classifyNets. Helpers: bdJsonPins.ts (pin and CONFIG.* parameter mapping, reusing INTERFACE_MODES, SCALAR_DIRECTIONS and SIGNAL_TYPES from bdTclCommands.ts; only parameters without value_src or with user) and bdJsonAddressing.ts (root addressing, 64K-style ranges to hex, is_excluded segments skipped with one info diagnostic). Source lines come from parsing the same text with yaml's LineCounter (JSON is valid YAML). An IP with vlnv is one block even when it carries components/nets; a component with reference_info.ref_name is a module; one without vlnv is a hier. isSystemDesignScript accepts a .bd file that matches "design": or starts with < (so the XML error reaches the user), readSystemDesign dispatches .bd, package.json adds *.bd to the ipcraft.systemDiagram selector, and detailsLabels.ts labels the format. SystemInstance.pinsComplete (set for .bd module references) makes isPinListKnown true; unconnectedPins() now skips the pins of any instance whose pin list is not known, InstanceDetails shows - instead of undriven / unused for them, and findingRow shows declared as the source of a pin on a pinsComplete instance. For block design scripts this removes a false finding: a pin of a block without a definition that a net of another level names (for example get_bd_pins hier/inner/pin at the root) is no longer listed as unconnected. Array parameter values (chunks Vivado splits at a space) are joined with a space. Tests: BdJsonReader.test.ts (fixture zynq_gpio_system.bd), BdJsonReader.realFiles.test.ts (set IPCRAFT_BD_SAMPLES to a folder of .bd files). (#300)
  • System viewer: search options and a result list in the outline. The new pure searchMatcher.ts compiles the query and SearchOptions (matchCase, wholeWord) once into a TextMatcher (compileSearch, null for a blank query): the trimmed query matches anywhere, * is any run of characters and ? one character (always on, other punctuation is literal), and whole word anchors a query edge that is an identifier character or a wildcard with (?<!\w) / (?!\w). matchesQuery, boundaryMatchesQuery, searchMatches, findSeed, minimapColor, useSearchStepper, useCanvasElements and the DiagramCanvas / DiagramMinimap props take the matcher (matcher: TextMatcher | null) in place of the query string, so the canvas dimming, minimap, counter, stepping and Ctrl+F seed agree. WorkbenchLayout holds the options and memoizes the matcher. The search input, its Match Case and Match Whole Word toggles and the counter moved from DiagramToolbar to the new SearchBox.tsx (one search prop). OutlineTree takes searchMatches (the stepper's matches, null without a search): it then renders only withAncestors(matches) (search.ts), every hierarchy open and without toggles, non-matching ancestors and the design row muted, no External ports group, the heading Search results, and No matching instances for none. A search that starts opens a collapsed outline once (effect on blank to non-blank in WorkbenchLayout). Tests: searchMatcher.test.ts, search.test.ts, panels.test.tsx, SystemDiagramApp.test.tsx. (#298)
  • System viewer: a filter box in the bottom panel. BottomPanel holds one filter text per BottomTab, compiles the text of the tab on show with compileSearch (default options) and passes the TextMatcher | null as filter to AddressMapTable, ClocksTable, ResetsTable, UnconnectedPinsTable and, through the Clocks and Resets tabs, CrossingsTable. The new pure panelFilter.ts owns what a row is matched against (segmentTexts, domainTexts, resetTexts, crossingTexts, findingTexts; a match in any cell keeps the row, addresses match as written and as grouped) and filterRows. The filter applies after the existing chips (Undriven/Unused, Show ... that could not be checked); tab counts and the crossing headline are not filtered; a table the filter empties shows NO_FILTER_MATCH. The tab strip is now a flex row holding the tablist and the input. Tests: panelFilter.test.ts, panels.test.tsx. (#298)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• System viewer: the compare picker no longer lists the current branch among the others. The git extension fills repository.state.HEAD asynchronously after it opens a repository; listRevisions (compare/gitRevisions.ts) read it before it was set, so the current branch could appear in the branch list (the cause of a flaky e2e run). It now calls repository.status() first when HEAD is not known. Tests: gitRevisions.test.ts. (#302)

  • System design diff: a connection change to a pin of a block in neither graph was hidden. isClassified in diffPins.ts counted every instance endpoint as classified, also a pin whose block exists in neither graph (for example sub/inner/clk under a black-box hierarchy whose proc is defined in another file, which the BD Tcl builder keeps as a net endpoint without an instance). The host rule then suppressed the pins it joined or left, and the report said No changes.. PinContext.instances (the instance paths of both graphs) now decides it. Tests: diffSystemGraphs.test.ts. (#307)

  • System viewer: starting or stopping a comparison no longer hides the problem banner. republish in SystemDiagramProvider posted the last valid graph, which clears the banner the webview shows when the document no longer reads as a design or fails to read. The provider now remembers the last notRecognized/error message (lastProblem, cleared by a published graph); republish reads it after its await, publishes the graph with the new comparison without pruning stored highlights, and posts the problem again. Tests: SystemDiagramProvider.test.ts. (#308)
  • System viewer marks: an address change on a version-only or renamed block is drawn as changed. buildChangeMarks kept the version or renamed status of a block whose address segment changed and only extended its tooltip, so a block whose address moved looked like one that differs only by the IP version. The status is now changed, with the title Changed: renamed from <old>, ... or Changed: <base type> → <current type>, .... Tests: changeMarks.test.ts, ChangeMarksPanels.test.tsx. (#309)
  • System design diff: values with line breaks or backticks no longer break the Markdown report. cell in diffReport.ts replaced only |, so a multi-line value (a Tcl CONFIG value, qsys CDATA) split its table row; line breaks are now written as one space. code always used single backticks, so a value containing a backtick ended its span early; the fence is now one backtick longer than the longest run in the text, padded with a space when the text starts or ends with a backtick (CommonMark). The golden reports are unchanged. Tests: diffReport.test.ts. (#302)
  • System design diff: peer lists are compared element by element. changeRows.ts compared the peers of a port with join() (comma), so a peer label that contains a comma could equal two peers; a small samePeers helper now serves the port and pin rows. Tests: changeRows.test.ts. (#302)
  • ipcraft diff: git errors name git's reason, and the current side is labelled with its revision. readGitFile in cli/gitFile.ts reported every rev-parse --show-prefix failure as "not in a git repository" and every git show failure as "does not exist at "; the messages keep that lead and now add the first line of git's stderr (a safe.directory refusal, a buffer overflow). With --head, the parse error of the current side in cli/diff.ts names <file> at <head>, like the base side. Tests: diff.node.test.ts. (#302)
  • System viewer compare: a default branch below a folder is not taken for the default branch. defaultBranch in gitRevisions.ts matched remote branches with endsWith('/main'), which also matched origin/feature/main; it now matches <remote>/<branch> (using remote of the git API ref when present, else the first path segment). Tests: gitRevisions.test.ts. (#302)
  • System viewer compare: the base picker shows progress and reads the open tab of a picked file. pickCompareBase.ts wraps the wait for the git extension (up to 3 s) in a status bar progress (Reading the git repository…), and Compare with File… uses the text of the picked file when it is open in an editor, as the open-design entries do, instead of the file on disk. Tests: pickCompareBase.test.ts. (#302)
  • System viewer compare: Marks comes back on whenever the base changes. useCompareView remembered only the last base Marks was turned off for, so off for X, switch to Y, back to X left it off; the toggle now resets on every change of baseLabel. Tests: useCompareView.test.tsx. (#302)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• System viewer: referenced but undefined blocks are black boxes. SystemInstance.kind gains 'blackbox' (referenced by a connection, an export or a call to a hierarchy proc defined elsewhere, not defined in the file read; pins are those seen in connections). SystemGraphBuilder.finish() (BD Tcl) adds one for every net endpoint whose instance does not exist and whose parent level does, so a cell created after its first connection stays a normal cell, and statement turns a create_hier_cell_<x> <parent> <name> call that is not a known proc into one (addBlackBox) instead of the "Ignored unrecognized command" info. buildQsysGraph (.qsys and qsys Tcl) adds a blackbox module for an undeclared, not disabled, module named by a connection or an export and keeps the connection or export; disabled modules are still dropped. Both emit one aggregated Not defined in this file, shown as a black box: ... warning in place of the per-connection "refers to unknown module" warnings. Consumers treat blackbox as a non-hierarchy leaf: instanceTypeLabel returns Black box (outline row and node subtitle), InstanceDetails explains it, the webview draws a dashed border (.sd-node[data-kind='blackbox']) and instanceSvg the equivalent stroke-dasharray, so the viewer, image export and ipcraft render agree. Definition matching (matchDefinitions, matchSubsystems) only considers ip and module instances and is unchanged; applyDefinitions counts a black box as an instance without a definition, so capabilities.unconnectedPins is partial when a design has one. Clock and reset analysis (physicalNets) treats a black box as a leaf end, so its clock inputs are loads. An empty name (missing qsys endpoint attribute, unresolved create_hier_cell_* name) never becomes a black box. (#291)
  • Port field metadata in .ip.yml. Optional fields on ports[] and busInterfaces[].conduitPorts[], and portFields: { <logicalName>: [...] } on bus interfaces, name bit ranges of a port (bits or offset/width, description, enumeratedValues). Metadata only: generators ignore it, and an integration test proves generated VHDL/SystemVerilog for Vivado and Quartus is byte-identical with and without it. apiVersion 1.2 is the latest format version (the 1.1 to 1.2 migration step only stamps the version). The Issues panel gets "Port fields" warnings (checkPortFields, source portFields) for the position form, range against the resolved width, overlap, duplicate names, enum values, and portFields keys that are unknown or not enabled. The fields follow the signal through group (standard, merge, single port, conduit), ungroup, map conduit to known bus, and save conduit as custom bus definition, each still one document update. Design: docs/concepts/port-fields.md. (#287)
  • Data Inspector: import from a port. The register-layout picker also lists ports with field metadata, grouped as Registers and Ports; the command is now Open Register or Port in Data Inspector (fpga-ip-core.openRegisterInDataInspector, id unchanged). DataInspectorRegisterLayoutReader also scans **/*.ip.yml and appends copyPortLayouts (src/dataInspector/portLayouts.ts), built on the new src/shared/portFields.ts (portFieldRange, enumeratePortFieldLists), which checkPortFields now shares; the bit-range parser moved to src/shared/bitRange.ts. RegisterLayoutCopy gains kind and provenance. importProvenance in data_inspector.schema.json is one of { sourceFile, registerName } or { sourceFile, portName, busInterface? }. Ports whose width does not resolve or exceeds 4096 bits are not offered. (#288)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • System viewer: boundary pins form two columns. boundaryNode (layout/elkLayout.ts) now sets ELK layer constraints from boundarySide through boundaryColumnOptions (both in the new layout/boundaryColumns.ts, with rightColumnDrivers): an input pin (east side) gets elk.layered.layering.layerConstraint: FIRST_SEPARATE and elk.alignment: LEFT, every other pin (output, inout, unknown direction) gets LAST_SEPARATE and RIGHT. FIRST/LAST are not used for the columns because a block could then share the first layer and sit left of the inputs. Inputs share a left edge left of every block, and the other ports share a right edge right of every block, for the root level, a hierarchy level shown as the level, an isolated view and a layout with expanded blocks (the inner level's pins are frame pins and unchanged). buildElkInput is shared, so the viewer, image export and ipcraft render change together. The kept clock or reset edge of placementEdges now only orders a clock or reset input port vertically next to a load. Layouts are up to about 275 px wider on the fixtures. A Platform Designer conduit export keeps its end/start convention as a fallback: definitionFromIpCore now derives a conduit bus interface's direction from its conduitPorts (all out -> master, all in -> slave, otherwise unknown), and the new pure pass applyExportDirections (enrichment/exportDirections.ts, run in enrichSystemGraph after applyDefinitions) gives a conduit export or unknown-direction boundary pin the direction its definition-backed instance endpoints agree on, with directionSource: 'definition'. Declared Vivado ports and disagreeing endpoints are unchanged. A conduit bus interface whose signals are all inputs or all outputs now has a pin direction instead of unknown, which can change which pin netDriver picks for a conduit net (wire direction, placement) and the unconnected-pin review (undriven vs unused). In boundaryNode, a right-column pin that drives another right-column pin (netDriver falls back to endpoints[0] for a net with no source endpoint) gets LAST (the last layer, which blocks can share) instead of LAST_SEPARATE because ELK throws on a LAST_SEPARATE node with an outgoing edge to another LAST_SEPARATE node; a pin that drives another such driver (a chain, where LAST to LAST throws too) is left unconstrained. Tests: external port columns (real ELK) in elkLayout.test.ts.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• System diagram first open no longer waits for enrichment. SystemDiagramProvider.postGraph races SystemDesignEnricher.enrich against ENRICHMENT_GRACE_MS (100 ms, src/providers/settleWithin.ts). If enrichment finishes first, one graph post as before; otherwise the parsed graph is posted with an info diagnostic "Resolving workspace definitions…", then the enriched graph. Both posts keep the sequence check; only the final post persists highlights. A setHighlights during the grace window keeps the stored highlights the early prune hid (instances only enrichment adds); "clear all" in that window keeps them. (#293)
  • Workspace index excludes before the limit. WorkspaceFileIndex passes an exclude glob to findFiles built by the pure buildExcludeGlob (enrichment/excludeGlob.ts) from the ignored directories of workspaceFilter.ts (now one list, also deriving isIgnoredWorkspacePath) and the true entries of search.exclude (one-level brace groups expanded; nested, unbalanced or stray braces skipped and logged). VS Code still applies files.exclude itself. isVisible matches the workspace-relative path against the same exclude, a files.exclude/search.exclude change drops the cached entries, and reaching the limit logs a warning. Applies to the .ip.yml, HDL and .qsys indexes. (#294)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• System viewer and image export: clock and reset nets are drawn as routed wires (#283). toFlowElements takes an optional IsolationSubset and, after the data wires, calls clockResetWires (layout/clockResetWires.ts), which builds terminals from the badge geometry (frame pin rows for an expanded block's inner level) and routes each level with layout/wireRoutes.ts (pure: block columns, channels, gaps, lanes, one tree per net cut into one polyline per sink). The wires are plain DiagramFlowEdges listed before the data wires, with ElkEdgeData.junction drawn as a dot by ElkEdge and systemLevelSvg. ELK still places the blocks from placementEdges only; elk.separateConnectedComponents is now false so the columns hold for the whole level. wireTree.ts holds the tree of one net.
