The frame of an expanded block is padded on each side (frameWireChannels in expandedLayout.ts, a lane per inner clock or reset net on that side, at least FRAME_WIRE_CHANNEL; frameLabelWidths gives the label widths) so its inner level has a wire channel beside the pin labels. JUNCTION_RADIUS is shared from diagramTypes.ts. cutWires gives a junction wire lead (the tree path from the driver to points[0], passed as ElkEdgeData.lead and drawn by ElkEdge before points), because onlyRenderVisibleElements culls each edge by its own two nodes and would drop trunk pieces other wires hang off; edgeMarks no longer dims clock and reset wires, whose leads overlap. Design: docs/concepts/clock-reset-wires.md.
  • System viewer: expanding or collapsing a hierarchy block in place keeps it at the same screen point (#285). useDiagramViewport remembers the previously shown layout; on a same-viewKey layout without a reveal it finds the flipped node with toggledNodeId and calls setViewport(anchoredViewport(...)) from a layout effect, so the first frame of the new layout has the corrected pan. Both helpers are pure functions in viewportPolicy.ts; decideViewportAction is unchanged.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • System viewer: highlighted nets keep selection-like emphasis (#241). ElkEdge gives a highlighted wire the selection width bump and an underlying sd-edge-halo path in the highlight color; highlightedEdgesLast (highlights.ts) orders highlighted edges after the others in useCanvasElements so they paint on top; NetBadgeView takes highlightColors (built by highlightedNetColors, set only on nodes found by badgedNodeIds) and colors the stub and label of clock and reset badges.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Transitive dependency advisories: non-breaking npm audit fix plus scoped overrides in package.json that lift nested minimatch (>=7 <11.0.1) to ^11.0.5 and glob (>=9 <14.0.2) to ^14.0.4. npm audit goes from 30 findings (1 critical, 5 high) to 6 low (deepmerge via jest-config, no patched release yet). (#280, #281)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• vhdl_ls.toml generation. ipcraft vhdl-ls [--root] [--dry-run] [--force] (src/cli/vhdlLs.ts, parseArgs in argv.ts, dispatched before resolveResourceRoots) and the trusted-only command fpga-ip-core.generateVhdlLsConfig (src/commands/VhdlLsConfigCommands.ts) share src/services/vhdlLsConfig/ (no vscode import): one fs walk with the enrichment exclusions plus Platform Designer <name>/synthesis|simulation (workspaceWalk.ts); readers for .xpr, .qsf/.qip, component.xml, _hw.tcl and .ip.yml (sourceReaders.ts); a light VHDL unit scanner; the pure rank, vendor-default (xil_defaultlib/work to defaultlib), duplicate and missing-library rules (buildLibraryMap.ts), with testbenches that reuse unit names split into a library each (scopeLibraries.ts), plus work.<unit> declarations shared across library boundaries (shareUnits.ts), one duplicate rule for generated libraries and proposals (duplicateRule.ts), user-section precedence (userLibraryFiles.ts), template files (${...} outside comments and strings) excluded by the scanner, and proposals by set cover over the units used with work. closure and exclude hints (proposeLibraryFiles.ts); rendering with a sha256 header over the generated section, an append-only user section and table-form proposals (renderVhdlLsToml.ts, userSection.ts, ownership.ts); vendor library files from ipcraft.vivado/quartus.installDirs by file system only (vendorLibraries.ts). The Tcl path word logic moved from HwTclParser to src/parser/tclPathWord.ts (resolveTclPathWord); flattenTclContent, SPIRIT_NS and normalizeXmlProlog are exported. New dependency toml (MIT). Tier-2 integration test runs vhdl_lang -c on generated fixtures (VHDL_LANG, REQUIRE_VHDL_LANG). Concept: docs/concepts/brainstorm/vhdl-ls-config.md. (#275)
  • Export image in the system viewer and the IP core editor. src/services/render/ is the Node-side render service shared by ipcraft render and the extension: renderSystemLevelImage (a resolved SystemLevelRequest plus RenderLook and ImageEncoding, with an optional cropNodeIds), renderIpSymbolImage (parsed .ip.yml plus the caller's bus library, with an optional crop rectangle), encodeImage, RenderAssets (fonts, bus libraries); isolateNodes and requireLevel moved there, closestNames too (cli/closestNames.ts re-exports it). The CLI keeps only name resolution (renderExpand.ts, renderSystemOptions.ts), the bus library loading (renderIpCore.ts) and file I/O; its outputs are byte-identical. renderSystemLevelSvg gained cropNodeIds (union of nodeBounds plus the margin) and renderIpSymbolSvg gained crop (intersected with the drawing). The extension bundle now loads dist/elk.bundled.js as an external, like the CLI. The webview posts typed exportImage messages (shared/messages/imageExport.ts, ExportImageOptions, sanitizeExportOptions) from the shared ExportImageButton popover; visibleNodeIds and buildSystemExportView (systemDiagram/exportView.ts, useDiagramExport) compute the system viewer's state, visibleLayoutRect (canvasGeometry.ts, useCanvasVisibleRect, useIpCoreExport) the IP canvas's visible rectangle. ImageExportHost renders, shows showSaveDialog, writes with workspace.fs, offers Open and Reveal in Explorer, and remembers the options in workspaceState (ipcraft.exportImage.<kind>); ExportTargets routes the fpga-ip-core.exportDiagramImage command to the active editor's webview. IsolatedView gained seedIds. (#268)
  • --workspace and --manifest for ipcraft render. The viewer's enrichment pipeline moved out of SystemDesignEnricher and SubsystemExpander into the pure services/systemDiagram/enrichment/enrichSystemGraph.ts (with expandSubsystems.ts, fileEntries.ts for the index entries, enrichmentIo.ts for the injected listIpFiles/listHdlFiles/listQsysFiles/readText); the two classes are now VS Code adapters (indexes, watchers, trust, vscode.workspace.fs) with unchanged behavior. cli/workspaceIo.ts is the Node adapter: a sorted directory walk with the same globs, limits, 1 MiB HDL cap and isIgnoredWorkspacePath, cached per directory in a WorkspaceIoPool. --workspace <dir> (default: the design's folder) and --no-workspace are rejected for an .ip.yml. --manifest <file.yml> (cli/renderManifest.ts, pure renderManifestSpec.ts) turns each entry into the argv of the equivalent render and runs it through parseRenderArgs, so the flag validators and messages are the single source of truth; defaults an entry cannot use are skipped. RenderSession (cli/renderResources.ts) shares fonts, bus libraries and workspace lists across a batch. (#268)
  • --select, --hops, --highlight and --clocks for ipcraft render. --select isolates blocks or port:<name> ports with their --hops neighbours (default 1, clamped to maxRadius) through the viewer's isolationSubset, passed to buildElkInput as isolate; --highlight draws the selected style without isolating (render argument parsing now lives in cli/renderArgv.ts; cli/renderSystemOptions.ts resolves names, with closestNames suggestions); --clocks runs analyzeClocks and clockDecor in domain mode. clockDecor.ts gained clockNodeData (now used by useCanvasElements) and applyClockDecor. The renderer gained selectedNodeIds and domainLegend options and decorSvg.ts; Palette gained focusBorder, warning, tokens and resolveColor. Output without these options is unchanged. (#268)
  • PNG and JPG output of ipcraft render. The --out extension picks the format (renderOutputFormat in argv.ts); --scale <1-4> (integer, default 2, rejected for .svg) and --quality <1-100> (default 90, JPG only); a transparent JPG is an argument error. src/shared/render/raster.ts rasterize runs @resvg/resvg-wasm 2.6.2 (MPL-2.0; wasm instance initialized once per process from bytes the CLI reads, so the glue never fetches) and, for JPG, encodes its RGBA pixels with jpeg-js 0.4.4 (BSD-3-Clause); both are exact-pinned runtime dependencies bundled into dist/cli.js, while the wasm is copied unmodified to dist/resources/resvg.wasm (ResourceRoots.resvgWasmPath, scripts/check-vsix.js, scripts/prepare-cli-package.js). The shipped fonts are now WOFF 1.0 (fontFaces.ts embeds font/woff); woffToSfnt.ts unwraps the same bytes to TrueType for resvg, which ignores @font-face. The VSIX budget is raised because the rasterizer ships in the VSIX. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md covers resvg-wasm and jpeg-js. (#268)
  • IP core symbol rendering. ipcraft render <file.ip.yml> --out <file.svg> [--theme] [--no-grid] [--background] (src/cli/renderIpCore.ts; --level, --expand and --no-legend are rejected for an .ip.yml in parseRenderArgs) draws the IP core canvas symbol with the new pure src/shared/render/ipSymbolSvg.ts and ipPortSvg.ts from computeLayout's CanvasLayout. The layout inputs (bus lookups, protocol labels, clock domain colors, isExpandableBus) moved from IpBlockCanvas.tsx into the pure canvas/symbolInputs.ts, shared by the canvas and the CLI; palette.ts gained the ip roles from canvas.css. The bus library is the built-in one plus the file's useBusLibrary folder (BusLibraryService, silent logger). (#268)
  • ipcraft render and the diagram renderer. ipcraft render <design.tcl|design.qsys> --out <file.svg> [--level] [--expand] [--theme] [--no-grid] [--no-legend] [--background] (src/cli/render.ts, runCliRender; parser parseRenderArgs in argv.ts; closestNames for the unknown-name suggestions) lays a level out with buildElkInput/runElkLayout/toFlowElements and draws it with the new pure renderer src/shared/render/ (systemLevelSvg.ts plus blockSvg.ts, pinSvg.ts, legendSvg.ts, svg.ts): native SVG only, no DOM, React, CSS or var(), deterministic bytes. palette.ts is the TypeScript source of truth for exported image colors (Light Modern and Dark Modern token values, color-mix roles computed by mixSrgb). Text is measured and drawn with IBM Plex Sans 400/600 and Mono 400 (OFL-1.1, @fontsource devDependencies copied to dist/resources/fonts, ResourceRoots.fontsDir): fontMetrics.generated.ts holds the advance widths (npm run generate:font-metrics, scripts/generate-font-metrics.js, fontkit as a devDependency) read by textMetrics.ts (measureText, plexTextMeasure), and fontFaces.ts embeds the woff2 files as base64 @font-face rules. layout/nodeHandles.ts no longer imports Position at runtime, so the CLI bundle carries no React. scripts/check-vsix.js, scripts/prepare-cli-package.js and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md cover the fonts. --expand accepts nested blocks (shownLevels). The layout engine ships once as dist/elk.bundled.js, copied by webpack, loaded by HtmlGenerator.generateSystemDiagramHtml before systemDiagram.js (external ELK) and required by dist/cli.js (external commonjs ./elk.bundled.js); prepare-cli-package.js also copies THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md into the CLI package. SVG only and whole system levels for now. (#268)
  • N-hop isolation in the system viewer. The isolated view has a radius (hops, 1 on every new isolation, session state in useIsolation). hopDistances runs one BFS over the data and interface edges of the level (clock and reset edges carry no hop); isolationSubset(graph, level, selected, hops) keeps the nodes within hops and the edges of any category between visible nodes where at least one is closer than hops, so N = 1 is the previous result, except when the reach is at most 1: then 1 hop is already the end point and the wires between two non-selected neighbours also show (maxRadius, the one value that bounds the stepper and triggers this rule). setHops clamps to [1, max(1, maxHops)] and bumps the token so the layout refits. DiagramCanvas is focusable (tabIndex=0, :focus-visible ring) and maps +/=/- through hopStepOfKey (hopKeys.ts) to onHopStep, ignored while typing and with Ctrl/Meta/Alt. The toolbar chip reads "Isolated · N selected · M of T shown" with a Fewer/More hops stepper (DiagramToolbar.tsx). (#266)
  • Minimap in the system viewer. A Minimap toggle in the toolbar's View group (codicon-map, off by default, session state) draws the React Flow MiniMap bottom right, pannable and zoomable, with selected blocks, search matches and hierarchy blocks colored (minimap.ts, DiagramMinimap.tsx). It is drawn only, never a layout input. (#265)
  • Auto detail in the system viewer. With the Simplify zoomed out toolbar toggle on (the default), zooming out below 0.42 hides pin labels, port labels, clock frequencies, block subtitles and badge text and enlarges block names by the inverse zoom, at most three times. It only changes what is drawn, so blocks never move. (#256)
  • Find keys in the system viewer. As in the VS Code text editor, Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on macOS) goes to Search instances with its text selected, filled in with the name of the selected block, and F3 or Shift+F3 goes to the next or previous match.
  • Search history in the system viewer. Up and Down in Search instances browse the remembered queries, as in the VS Code find box (placeholder Search instances (⇅ for history)): a query is remembered when stepping (Enter, Shift+Enter, F3, Shift+F3) or on blur, deduplicated, at most 50, for the session. Pure rules in searchHistory.ts, state in hooks/useSearchHistory.ts. (#264)
  • Mouse forward button in the system viewer. After going up with the mouse back button, the mouse forward button returns to the levels you left, one at a time. Going to another level any other way clears them, as in a browser.
  • Clock and reset domains in the system viewer. The Clocks and resets toggle colors the clock and reset pins by clock domain, shows the clock frequencies set in the design, and marks clock and reset domain crossings (CDC and RDC). Selecting a clock or reset net shows its whole tree in Details. New Clocks and Resets tabs list the domains, reset sources and crossings of the level on screen; clicking a row zooms to it. Clocks are identified from known AMD IP outputs and declared pin directions, never from pin names, and what cannot be determined is listed as not checked. Known outputs of common AMD IPs are now drawn on the right of their block. (#243, #248, #252)
  • Expand a hierarchy block in place in the system viewer. The + button in the header of a hierarchy block (or right-click, Expand In-Place) shows its contents in a frame on the current level; the - button or Collapse folds it again. Double-click still opens the block. (#244, #247)
  • Highlight and multi-select in the system viewer. Cmd+Click (macOS) or Ctrl+Click (other systems) selects several blocks, ports and wires at once, and right-click, Highlight, marks them in one of six colors. Highlights are kept per design file, a toolbar chip counts them and clears them all, and they pause while the Unconnected pins review is on. (#241, #254)
  • Review unconnected pins in the system viewer. The Unconnected pins toggle marks pins that no net touches, undriven inputs in the warning color and unused outputs muted, and lists them in an Unconnected tab. Only blocks with a known pin list (an .ip.yml or HDL definition, hierarchy pins, external ports) are checked. (#245, #246, #251)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• System viewer toolbar in the IP core editor style. ToolbarGroup and ToolbarSeparator move from IpCoreToolbar.tsx to src/webview/shared/components/Toolbar.tsx, where a group now has role="group" and its label as accessible name, and the .canvas-view-toggle button styles move from the IP core canvas.css to shared/components/toolbar.css. The system viewer toolbar uses them for icon-only Design (Clocks and resets pulse, Unconnected pins debug-disconnect), View (Simplify zoomed out text-size, zoom-out, Fit screen-full, zoom-in) and Panels groups; accessible names are unchanged. (#264)
  • Shorter wires in the system viewer. Blocks are placed by their data and interface connections, external ports sit next to a block they connect to, and clock and reset nets are shown as net-name badges on their pins instead of wires; large designs lay out much faster. (#261)
  • Blocks stand out from the canvas in the system viewer. Blocks have a darker outline, a tinted body and header, and a light shadow; wires are thinner and softer until selected or highlighted, and the grid dots are fainter. (#261)
  • Clocks and resets is a toggle button in the system viewer. It colors the clock and reset pins by clock domain, and a count chip next to it opens the Clocks tab. (#258, #259)
  • Clicking an unconnected pin zooms in to its block in the system viewer when the block is too small to read. (#245, #249)
  • Stronger block outlines in the system viewer on light and dark themes. (#244, #247)
  • No Problems tab in the system viewer. It listed what the offline reader could not resolve, which read like faults in the design. Details still summarizes what the offline view cannot know. (#250)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• System viewer responds faster on large designs. On the 64-channel vivado_dsp_soc_64ch root level (228 blocks, 480 wires, production build): (1) AutoDetail.tsx writes --sd-name-scale only while far and in NAME_SCALE_STEP (0.25) steps (farNameScale in layout/zoomDetail.ts), so a zoom gesture no longer restyles the whole canvas on every frame; (2) hooks/useCanvasElements.ts (extracted from DiagramCanvas.tsx) keeps the node and edge objects of elements that draw the same thing (reuseUnchanged in stableElements.ts, via hooks/useStableElements.ts), so React Flow skips them: selectedNetIds and review objects reach only the nodes they concern, onSelectNet is stable, and the clock decor is rebuilt only when the selection is a clock or reset net; (3) dimming (search and clock or reset tree) is the node className sd-dimmed on the React Flow wrapper instead of data.dimmed, and InstanceNode, FrameNode and BoundaryNode are React.memo, so a block that is only dimmed or undimmed keeps its data object and does not render its pins again; (4) <ReactFlow> sets onlyRenderVisibleElements, so the blocks and wires off screen are not mounted, and toFlowElements gives every node measured (its layout size) and handles (the source and target handle of each pin, built by layout/nodeHandles.ts from the ELK port geometry, the same set the node components render): without measured React Flow drops the handle bounds of every node whose object changes and then mounts that node again even off screen, and with measured alone it would keep stale handle ids (a renamed pin lost its wire) because it would never read them again (zoomed in on 24 of 228 blocks, a keystroke mounted 175 of them). Fit mounts the whole design again and costs more (script 40 ms to about 80 ms). Measured with npm run perf:system-viewer (64ch; script time unless noted): a keystroke 120-165 ms to 19-21 ms, selecting a block 144 ms to 8 ms, 10 wheel zoom steps 471 ms to 57 ms of style recalculation, drag pan 259 ms to 31 ms, zoomed in a keystroke 6-7 ms with the 24 visible blocks mounted; no long task on any keystroke, selection, zoom or pan (Fit has one of about 150-180 ms). The two commits per keystroke are React Flow's own (its store update after the parent render, also seen with a plain <ReactFlow>), not ours. The measurement script is scripts/perf/system-viewer.spec.ts (config/playwright.perf.ts). (#267)
  • The system viewer fills the editor. systemDiagram.css now resets the body padding that VS Code's default webview stylesheet adds (20px each side), as src/webview/index.css already does for the other editors, so the toolbar and canvas reach both edges. (#264)
  • Blocks no longer move in the system viewer when Clocks and resets or Unconnected pins is turned on or off; the zoom and pan stay too. (#255, #257)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Isolate blocks in the system viewer. Cmd+Click (macOS) or Ctrl+Click (other systems) adds blocks and ports to the selection, and right-click, Isolate N Selected (Isolate Selection for a single block) shows only them, the wires that touch them, and the blocks at the other end of those wires, laid out compactly. Show All, in the right-click menu or the toolbar, restores the full view and its zoom and pan.
  • Mouse back button goes up a level. In the system viewer, the mouse back button goes up one hierarchy level, like clicking the parent in the breadcrumb.
  • Search steps through matches. In the system viewer, Enter and Shift+Enter in the search box go to the next and previous match on any hierarchy level, centring it (and zooming in if it is small) with a brief pulse. A counter shows the position, and Escape clears the search.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • System viewer restyled. Blocks get a header band (hierarchy blocks a dashed outline and an OPEN hint), clock and reset labels are quieter and drop the driver instance prefix from their names, a legend names the wire categories on screen, the outline and details panels follow the side bar theme, and the address map shows grouped hex addresses and humanized ranges. Pin markers sit on the block border with wires ending at them (unconnected pins are italic with a hollow marker, pins on the selected net are bold), and external ports are arrow tags.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Platform Designer subsystems open as hierarchy levels. A .qsys module whose kind names another .qsys file in the workspace is read into the system viewer as a hierarchy level, so double-clicking it enters the subsystem, with the breadcrumb and outline, also for nested subsystems. Its blocks get the same .ip.yml and HDL pins as top-level blocks, and go-to-source opens the subsystem file at the right line. Subsystems that instantiate each other, and subsystem files that cannot be read, are listed in Problems and stay a plain block. Subsystems are not read in untrusted workspaces.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Offline system viewer. IPCraft: Open as System Diagram (Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V on a recognized .tcl or .qsys file toggles it) opens a Vivado write_bd_tcl script, a Platform Designer .qsys (Standard) system, or a Platform Designer system script (qsys-script .tcl) as a read-only diagram. Files are read statically and never executed, so no vendor tool or license is needed. The diagram shows one hierarchy level at a time with an outline and search, details, an address map, and problems; clocks and resets are pin badges until Clocks and resets is turned on; zoom and pan are kept per level. Workspace .ip.yml files (by VLNV or Platform Designer component name) and HDL files (for Vivado module references) add unconnected pins, directions, interface types and a Defined by link, and are not read in untrusted workspaces. Address ranges from definitions are not filled in yet. Platform Designer scripts usually leave out the connection type, so it is inferred from parameters, other connections and interface names, and anything inferred by name or left unknown is listed in Problems. Blocks size to their pin names, hovering a pin shows its full name, direction and nets, double-clicking a block zooms to it and double-clicking empty canvas fits the level, the side and bottom panels start hidden, and a temporarily broken edit keeps the last valid design on screen with a banner. See Viewing a System Design. (#239)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Bus port presence follows the protocol specs. AXI4-Stream TREADY, Avalon-ST valid, and AXI4-Lite and AXI4 AWPROT/ARPROT are now optional, so they are generated only when listed in useOptionalPorts. New rules reject inconsistent port sets: on AXI4, AWID with BID, ARID with RID, AWLEN needs WLAST and ARLEN needs RLAST; on Avalon-MM, read needs readdata, write needs writedata, readdatavalid needs read, writeresponsevalid needs response, and beginbursttransfer needs burstcount.
  • The VSIX now bundles the elkjs layout engine (EPL-2.0, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), and the VSIX size budget is raised to 25 MiB unpacked and 2.5 MiB compressed.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: • Interfaces that relied on TREADY, valid, AWPROT or ARPROT being generated implicitly no longer get those ports, which changes the generated HDL, component.xml and _hw.tcl. Add them to the interface's useOptionalPorts to keep the previous ports. An Avalon-MM or AXI4 interface whose ports break one of the new presence rules now fails validation until the missing port is added.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Self-contained IP packages. The new IPCraft: Package IP Core (Self-Contained) command and ipcraft package <ip.yml> --out <path> [--zip] bundle an .ip.yml with every file it references (memory map and file-set imports, file-set files, the useBusLibrary file or folder, and subcores with a path, transitively) into a folder or .zip. Files outside the IP directory are copied under deps/ and their references are rewritten in place, so all other files stay byte-identical. Missing files, path conflicts and symlink loops are reported together before anything is written. (#234)
  • Bit fields can be added with the mouse. The fields table shows a hover insert bar (+) at gaps where a free bit exists, and the field-table and visualizer context menus offer Insert Above/Below and Insert Before/After. The new field's name cell is focused. An insert that would shift an existing field is rejected with an error instead. (#235)
  • Regeneration tells hand edits from generator changes. IPCraft records what it last generated under <output>/.ipcraft/baseline and classifies each modified file against it. Both staging views offer per-file Auto-merge (clean three-way merge), Sync interface (replace only the entity/module header), Overwrite and Keep. Hand-edited and locked files default to Keep or Auto-merge, never Overwrite. The merge editor uses the baseline as its base, and the baseline is updated when a merge is saved. Locked (managed: false) files that already exist now appear in staging when their interface is out of date; they are still never written without an explicit choice. (#236)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The "Generation failed" message shows the first conformance issue.
  • New registers created in the Memory Map editor no longer get an explicit access: read-write.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Generated register files compile when register-level access disagrees with the field accesses. For example, the editor's old default access: read-write over read-only fields produced VHDL and SystemVerilog that did not compile. Field accesses now decide the access of a register that has fields; register-level access applies only to field-less registers, in the HDL, component.xml, memmap.yml and docs. Dead W1C write branches are no longer emitted. The template context contract is now 1.5.0 and adds write_fields, needs_write_branch and read_source per register. (#238)
  • A workspace IP-XACT bus definition without an IPCraft contract, such as the avalon_mm.xml that Vivado packaging exports, no longer replaces the builtin definition with the same VLNV. Before, it turned a memory-mapped slave into a conduit and blocked generation. It is now skipped with a BUS_DEF_CONTRACTLESS_OVERRIDE_IGNORED warning.
  • Resizing or moving a bit field masks its reset value to the new width, so a bit that no longer fits does not come back when the field grows again. Files already saved with an out-of-range reset value display consistently. (#237)
  • After a Ctrl+Drag of a bit field, the fields table no longer keeps a stale drag preview that froze its Bit(s) cell and hid later Shift+Drag resizes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: • Generated HDL changes for registers whose register-level access disagrees with their fields. Such output did not compile before, so no working design is affected. The template context contract keys are additive, so custom packs declaring apiVersion: "^1.x" keep working; a pack pinned with ~1.4 or an exact 1.4.0 must widen its range.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Bus interfaces are now checked against one canonical contract library across the editor, importers, consistency checks, and generators. The Issues panel groups protocol errors and warnings, links them to the affected canvas signal and Inspector field, and blocks generation when a known error or unresolved generation constraint remains.
  • Configurable port polarity. A bus contract can declare an active-high and an active-low role for the same logical port, and an interface selects one per port through portPolarityOverrides. The Inspector exposes a per-port polarity selector, the canvas marks the resolved role, and vendor artifacts (_hw.tcl, IP-XACT) carry the polarity-specific interface role while generated HDL keeps canonical active-high internals and inverts at the boundary. Only a nondefault choice is stored; returning a port to its contract default removes the entry. Avalon-MM byteenable, readdatavalid, waitrequest, read, and write are polarity-configurable, replacing the separate _n logical ports, which are still accepted when reading existing documents.
  • The extension now ships the ipcraft CLI and puts it on PATH. It is available in VS Code integrated terminals automatically, and IPCraft: Install 'ipcraft' Command in PATH installs it for external terminals on this machine without sudo or Node.js. CI runners without VS Code are not covered. (#206)
  • Platform Designer _hw.tcl import understands real-world Tcl. The importer now resolves Tcl variables, expands for/foreach loops with literal or parameter bounds (up to 256 iterations), reduces [expr ...] widths, binds proc argument defaults, treats [log2ceil X] as clog2(X), and runs elaboration callbacks so TERMINATION, WIDTH/WIDTH_EXPR, -1 placeholder widths and zero-width optional ports produce the real interface. Legacy add_port_to_interface ports take their direction and width from the Verilog module named by set_module. Names and widths that still contain Tcl syntax are dropped with a warning instead of being imported verbatim, and the import command shows a summary of the warnings. Across the 1,133 _hw.tcl files shipped with Quartus 25.1, none now import with Tcl syntax in a name or width (408 did before). (#212, #213, #214)
  • ipcraft migrate and the editor's Migrate command bring more documents up to date. They rename legacy snake_case keys to camelCase in .ip.yml and .mm.yml files, keeping comments, key order and hex spellings; rewrite dotted bus-type VLNVs written for the IPCraft Python CLI (ipcraft.busif.axi4_lite.1.0) to the canonical colon form; and repair a dangling memoryMapRef when the intended map is unambiguous. ipcraft migrate --check reports each of these. (#229, #230, #232)
  • The Inspector's Port Widths section shows AXI-Stream TUSER, so its width can be viewed and overridden. Other 1-bit signals that the bus definition fixes stay hidden. (#208)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Avalon-MM now uses its canonical logical port set and optionality in the canvas and generated artifacts. Legacy aliases are accepted only at the document boundary and resolve to the canonical IPCraft VLNV.
  • Avalon-ST uses source and sink modes and preserves dataBitsPerSymbol, symbolsPerBeat, readyLatency, maxChannel, and endianness through Platform Designer Tcl and custom IP-XACT. Big-endian generated RTL reverses Avalon-ST data in symbol-sized lanes; AXI, Avalon-MM, and standalone ports retain eight-bit lanes.
  • A bus interface with no physicalPrefix now generates unprefixed port names (awaddr, address, ...) in the Inspector, the canvas, and every generated artifact. Previously every non-conduit interface fell back to s_axi_ regardless of its type, so an AXI-Stream master or a FIFO interface got AXI-style names that the canvas never showed. The duplicate-port check now also covers prefix-less interfaces and authored conduitPorts.
  • The AXI4-Lite and Avalon-MM bus wrappers name their internal signals <logical>_int (for example awaddr_int), so a prefix-less slave elaborates instead of colliding with its own ports. Port names and register-bank signals are unchanged.
  • IPCraft reads camelCase keys only. The editor, validator and generators no longer fall back to legacy snake_case spellings such as bus_interfaces, memory_maps or file_sets. Before, a file containing both spellings showed one value in the editor and generated from the other. Convert older files with IPCraft: Migrate .ip.yml / .mm.yml to Latest Format or ipcraft migrate. The bundled schema also rejects unknown keys on bus interfaces and ports.
  • The Upgrade command is now IPCraft: Migrate .ip.yml / .mm.yml to Latest Format. It runs the same migration as ipcraft migrate, is offered for .mm.yml files in the Explorer and the Command Palette, and works from a text editor or a visual editor tab. Its command ID is unchanged, so existing keybindings keep working.
  • Failed bus-contract rules are explained in plain language. Each message names the interface and states the current and expected values where they are known, and warnings say that they are non-blocking recommendations. Before, a message read only <RULE_ID> is not satisfied.
  • The bus library is loaded once and cached until a bus definition, busLibraryPaths, the Vivado version or the workspace scan changes, which makes repeated validation and editor refreshes much faster with large Vivado interface catalogs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Generated AXI4-Lite slaves (VHDL and SystemVerilog) no longer lose a transaction or deadlock when the master offers several at once. The wrapper accepted the next write's W beat while the previous write response was still pending (overwriting the latched write data) and the next AR while RVALID was still pending (that read was never answered). It now takes one write and one read at a time. Masters with transactions in flight, such as an AXI SmartConnect forwarding posted PCIe writes, hit this; on a PCIe host the hung slave caused completion timeouts. A new behavioral suite (axil-handshake, GHDL and Icarus Verilog) offers write and read transactions back to back.
  • Format-preserving writes no longer reformat untouched YAML. Before, any edit, deletion or migration re-rendered the whole document, so flow lists gained padding ([TLAST] became [ TLAST ]) and folded block scalars were joined onto one line. CRLF line endings are kept. (#231)
  • A bus interface whose memoryMapRef names a missing memory map now blocks generation. Before, IPCraft accepted it and wrote a dangling reference into component.xml. (#232)
  • Generated Vivado component.xml passes check_integrity in more cases. Avalon-MM port maps use the uppercase logical names Xilinx declares for avalon_rtl. Ports that the Xilinx abstraction does not declare become plain component ports. The generic IPCraft conduit is emitted as plain ports instead of an unresolvable bus interface. Authored conduitPorts on a library bus type map only the logical ports that the type declares. (#215, #225)
  • A conduit with a full VLNV bus type that cannot be resolved and has no conduitPorts now blocks generation, because its ports would otherwise be missing from component.xml. The generic ipcraft:busif:conduit:1.0 placeholder and conduits with authored ports are still accepted. (#226)
  • component.xml import reads address-block ranges written with a size suffix (4K) correctly, maps Xilinx Avalon interfaces back to IPCraft Avalon-MM with correct port directions and widths, and keeps the Avalon ports that avalon_rtl lacks across a round trip. (#224)
  • component.xml no longer contains an empty ipcraft:interfaceContract element for a bus interface whose contract declares nothing to record. (#217)

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • Updated the bundled @xmldom/xmldom (0.9.12), js-yaml (4.3.2) and fast-uri (3.1.8) to versions that fix published denial-of-service and injection advisories.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Bus-interface compatibility is forward-only for port polarity. This version reads every bus-interface document the 1.0.0 release supported, and existing active-high documents keep their behavior and generated port names. A document that selects an active-low port through portPolarityOverrides requires this version or later: an older IPCraft ignores the field and would generate the active-high role instead.
  • An existing IP that relied on the implicit s_axi_ prefix now gets unprefixed port names in the generated HDL, component.xml, _hw.tcl, and the cocotb testbench, which breaks instantiations that use the old names. Set physicalPrefix: s_axi_ on the interface to keep them.
  • Documents that still use snake_case keys, or the bus_interfaces root alias, must be migrated once with the Migrate command or ipcraft migrate. Until they are, the legacy keys are ignored and the schema reports them.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Multi-version Vivado/Quartus toolchain support lets you register several installed versions (and Docker images) per vendor, auto-detects which one an existing project needs from a .ipcraft-toolchain.json sidecar or by parsing the project file, and lets you force a specific version at any time via the new IPCraft: Select Vivado Version / Select Quartus Version commands. (#202)
  • Automated Marketplace releases. Starting with this version, IPCraft is published through a protected GitHub Actions workflow with immutable versioned artifacts, SHA-256 verification, VS Code minimum/stable smoke tests, and passwordless Azure identity federation, replacing manual VSIX uploads. (#201)
  • SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SUPPORT.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md document the vulnerability reporting process, contributor setup, and support channels. (#200)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• IP Core toolbar buttons ("Open in Platform Designer", "Edit in IP Packager") now refresh immediately after Generate/Export/vendor-project commands instead of staying greyed out until the editor is closed and reopened.
  • The Vivado/Quartus version picker no longer self-closes on the first click when triggered from a webview toolbar button.
  • Vendor project launch workflows no longer show a spurious, seemingly concurrent version-picker prompt when Vivado and Quartus projects are scaffolded together.
  • Generation with an out-of-tree fileSets path (e.g. ../src/pkg.vhd, common in Qsys/Platform Designer layouts) no longer aborts the whole scaffold; only paths meant to be written are checked for output-directory containment. (#204)
  • The README demo now embeds an animated GIF instead of an unsupported <video> tag, so it renders on the VS Code Marketplace and in the editor's Markdown preview, not just on GitHub.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Product demo video in the README provides a quick walkthrough of IPCraft's visual editing and generation workflow.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Generator template context 1.3.0 adds authored parameter page/group layouts for Vivado xGUI and Quartus Platform Designer, including Tcl-safe parameter metadata for custom scaffold packs.
  • Extension and CLI release versions are synchronized at 0.9.9.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Vertical bit-field rulers now show an aligned index for every bit, including gaps, instead of labeling only segment endpoints. (#192)
  • Generation from edited IP cores now uses the current unsaved editor snapshot for previews and output while leaving generated YAML metadata changes unsaved for review. (#197)
  • Quartus parameter layout round-trips now preserve authored uiPage and uiGroup hierarchy, labels, defaults, and Tcl string values in generated and imported Platform Designer components. (#193, #194)
  • Quartus generated filesets retain their resolved RTL paths instead of adding an extra parent-directory prefix. (#198)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Project documentation now presents IPCraft's workflow and benefits more clearly, separates exploratory design concepts from implementation references, and describes the current LED Avalon-MM example without retaining development-history reports.
  • Extension and CLI release versions are synchronized at 0.9.8.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Compound extensions in create dialogs are preserved when users enter names such as example.ip.yml, registers.mm.yml, or Data Inspector recipe filenames, preventing duplicated or truncated suffixes. (#190)
  • IP Core canvas zoom indicator remains visible throughout consecutive wheel events and hides after zooming stops instead of resetting its fade state during an active gesture. (#186)
  • Imported VHDL zero-based widths now retain their parameter expression when a range uses forms such as WIDTH downto 0 without a trailing - 1. (#188)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Semantic cocotb register verification: generated testbenches now use a resolved verification manifest and software register model to check reset values, access modes, reserved bits, byte enables, unmapped reads, write-1-to-clear and self-clearing behavior, and deterministic randomized traffic across AXI and Avalon transports. (#180)
  • Generated interrupt associations: interrupt ports now carry bus and clock associations through the schema, canvas Inspector, generated RTL, template context, and Platform Designer output, with validation for invalid references. (#183)
  • Unified DE10-Nano conformance flows: the Avalon-MM and AXI4-Lite examples share manifest-driven scenarios between cocotb simulation and hardware validation; the Avalon-MM project now supports both Nios II and Nios V systems. (#181)
  • Generator design references: added a feature-coverage matrix and an implementation-scoped architecture proposal for inferred RAM buffers. (#179)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Open-source integration CI now runs all applicable suites on pull requests and uses a dedicated nightly workflow, so newly added open-source integration groups are included automatically. (#178)
  • Marketplace publishing metadata now targets the bahonavi publisher and includes expanded FPGA protocol and vendor keywords.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• IP Core canvas titles now wrap and preserve stable layout measurements instead of overflowing or clipping long names.
  • Getting Started walkthrough accuracy: corrected scaffold-pack defaults and file ownership, memory-map bus attachment, canvas-side semantics, report navigation, generated VHDL and cocotb examples, target selection, clock-frequency behavior, and vendor-import limitations.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Configurable generated-file indentation: select the indentation used for generated HDL and tool files through IPCraft settings or the CLI; scaffold packs can declare a per-pack default. (#162)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Generated register access modes: explicit access modes declared on registers are now preserved during HDL generation.
  • Consistency Check top-level selection: testbenches and black-box stubs no longer cause false interface-drift reports; when IPCraft cannot choose a unique implementation, it reports an informational ambiguity instead. (#163)
  • Data Inspector canvas edits: semantically invalid edits remain visible and are retained until corrected, rather than disappearing; new sources inherit the current input width for compatible binary operations. (#165)
  • IP Core canvas drag handling: malformed drag payloads are rejected before they can change the canvas.
  • Memory Map mutations: structural insert and delete operations no longer mutate their input state, preventing stale UI state from being modified. (#170)
  • Register value input: hexadecimal values now consistently use the 0x prefix.
  • Bus definition scanning: invalid cached scan results are ignored and refreshed instead of being reused.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Scaffold-pack generation contracts: packs can declare compatible HDL languages, bus types, memory-mapped-slave requirements, and required logical ports; incompatible inputs now fail before rendering in both generate and verify. Pack file rules can also request POSIX executable bits for generated helper scripts. (#152, #153, #154)
  • Scaffold-pack template filters: registered identifier casing (snakecase, camelcase, pascalcase, constcase), log2, ljust, and latexescape filters for custom Nunjucks templates. (#155)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Avalon-ST Platform Designer symbol-order metadata is now derived from interface endianness, replacing the separate firstSymbolInHighOrderBits schema field and Inspector checkbox. (#145)
  • Data Inspector bit lanes now use a compact layout and concise provenance labels when no field overlay is present.
  • Webview architecture: decomposed the Data Inspector application root and the IP Core canvas, inspector, toolbar, interaction, and session state into focused components and hooks with direct regression coverage. User-visible editing, selection, staging, and synchronization behavior is preserved. (#128, #129, #130)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Full-generation scaffold-pack ownership: packs can explicitly disable IPCraft's framework testbench, and packs inferred to own their complete output tree no longer receive unrelated tb/, .vscode/settings.json, docs/, altera/, or xilinx/ files. Staging identifies framework-owned files, ambiguous packs receive actionable warnings, and generate and verify remain aligned. (#151, #156)
  • Quartus SystemVerilog endian-swap generation: generated byte-reordering loops now use explicit generate blocks and separately declared genvar identifiers accepted by Quartus, while remaining compatible with other synthesis and simulation tools.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Configurable port and bus endianness: standalone vector ports and built-in bus data paths can be marked big-endian. Generated VHDL and SystemVerilog reflow data bytes and their qualifier masks together, including parameterized widths and stream-only designs.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The public generator template-context contract is now version 1.1.0 with additive endian-swap metadata. Packs using a ~1.0 API range must update to ~1.1 (or a compatible caret range) after validating the new context.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Reset polarity and interrupt sensitivity on the IP canvas: reset ports now distinguish active-high and active-low signals with polarity badges and inversion bubbles, while interrupt ports show compact level/edge sensitivity markers with accessible labels and tooltips. (#135)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Production VSIX packages now exclude nested source maps and are checked in CI against an explicit runtime-content allowlist and size budget. The checked artifact is installed for extension-host smoke testing. (#123)
  • Native, accessible webview controls: replaced the deprecated VS Code Webview UI Toolkit with shared React controls backed by native form elements, preserving Vim table navigation and restoring inspector empty-state contrast. (#124)
  • Documentation refresh: consolidated overlapping architecture and concept material, added task-focused guides for creating, importing, generating, and checking IP cores, and added reproducible screenshot-backed documentation with automated link validation.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• CLI distribution contract: removed the unavailable npx ipcraft claim from Marketplace-facing documentation and separated the ipcraft npm artifact from the VSIX. The CLI can now be packed and smoke-tested from a clean temporary installation without publishing; npm publication remains an explicit manual release after the matching extension release. (#116)
  • Legacy memory-map editing and serialization: legacy snake-case input is now normalized only at the document boundary while the runtime model remains canonical camelCase. Structural and scalar edits resolve the original on-disk keys without creating duplicate sections, and opaque enum/custom-metadata maps survive normalization and serialization unchanged. (#119)
  • Workspace and webview security boundaries: generation, build, vendor-tool, template, and external-process actions are disabled in untrusted workspaces; scaffold output paths are contained within their target directory; and every webview now declares the minimum local resource roots it needs. (#121)
  • IP canvas layout stability: preserved measured node dimensions across layout updates so selections and refreshes no longer collapse nodes back to default sizes.
  • Bus-library navigation: section headers remain visible while scrolling through long IP Core library groups. (#137)
  • Avalon-ST signal ordering: the IP canvas now recognizes Avalon Streaming symbol order so data, channel, error, and empty signals are presented in their defined order. (#136)
  • VS Code 1.80 compatibility: pinned extension API types to the declared minimum engine version and added automated compatibility checks to prevent newer API usage from entering supported builds.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Data Inspector: a new standalone tool for decoding an arbitrary-width value — pasted from a waveform, an ILA/SignalTap capture, a register read, or typed by hand — into named bit fields, without ever touching .mm.yml/.ip.yml or HDL generation. Three new commands: IPCraft: Open Data Inspector (a temporary inspection panel), IPCraft: Open Register in Data Inspector (pre-loads a register's field layout from a workspace memory map), and IPCraft: New Data Inspector (creates a reusable *.ipci.yml recipe with its own custom editor). Values are modeled as four-state bit vectors (0/1/X/Z, not plain integers), so numeric interpretations correctly report "unknown bits" instead of silently showing a wrong number when a range contains an unresolved bit. Accepts Verilog (32'hDEAD_BEEF), VHDL (x"0123_ABCD"), and C-style (0xDEADBEEF) literals, decimal, and binary, all with underscore digit separators. Supports multiple named sources composed via transform steps (concat, slice, bitwise and/or/xor/not, shift left/right, zero/sign-extend, truncate, byte swap), field overlays with hex/binary/unsigned/signed/enum/float/fixed-point interpretation and an expected-value pass/fail check, VCD signal timelines and CSV/ILA sample import (configurable radix, byte order, word order), and lane-width/zoom (overview, by-field, by-bit) controls with keyboard navigation. A saved recipe holds sources, fields, transforms, and view settings, but deliberately never the pasted value or capture history. (#107)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Fields table access column redesign: the Memory Map fields table's access-mode dropdown now shows short SVD-style tokens (RO/WO/RW/W1C/RW1C/WSC/RWSC) when closed, with full names only in the open listbox, and the popup consistently opens downward and sizes to its content instead of occasionally misdirecting near the viewport edge. The W1C Monitors sub-row (which broke row-height uniformity) is replaced by a compact icon button opening an anchored picker menu.
  • Data Inspector internals decomposed: the Data Inspector webview's monolithic app component was split into focused hooks (value input/literal parsing, capture import, field panel state, host sync, recipe autosave) and presentational components (value composer, capture panel, field panel), with direct unit test coverage added for each extracted hook, including the host-sync revision protocol. No user-visible behavior change. (#112)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Data Inspector debug-mode overrides and value-bar validation: a bit field defined via the common offset/width schema form lost a committed debug-mode override wider than 53 bits on the very next render (the reapplication only ran in the fallback code path); and the value-bar's parser collapsed malformed, out-of-range, and empty drafts into a single generic "Value is required" message instead of reporting which one actually happened.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Compact register and register-array editing: removed the register-card rail from the block and register-array editors — selection, insert, delete, and drag-reorder already existed in the Outline panel, and the rail's fixed width squeezed the fields table on narrow screens (e.g. a 13" laptop). Keyboard insert/delete (o/O/Shift+A/Shift+I/d/Delete) and inline editing of a register's name, offset, and description moved onto the Outline and a new compact register header strip so nothing the rail did was lost; register and array rows also gained a color swatch, and array count/stride became double-click-editable directly on the row. The now-unused RegisterMapVisualizer was removed, the bit-field visualizer's default pane width shrank from 340px to 240px to match, its cells were flattened to match the memory map visualizer's style, and ValueBar was resized to fit the narrower pane. (#99)
  • Register Value/Hex input moved to the fields toolbar: lifted from the bottom of the (now-removed) bit-field rail to sit level with the field move-up/move-down buttons at the top of the fields table, in both the side-by-side and stacked layouts. (#105)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Outline readability and navigation: base-address, offset, count, and stride labels in the Memory Map outline were too small to read (10px, now matching the app's standard size); the footer's item count and "Base: 0x0" no longer ignore the current selection and instead reflect whatever level is selected (blocks, registers, or fields); and an implicit horizontal scrollbar — caused by overflow-y: auto also enabling overflow-x, per the CSS spec — no longer clips row content sideways; names now truncate with an ellipsis instead. (#101, #102)
  • RTL compile order still wrong in some fallback cases: the topological-sort fix shipped in 0.9.0 (above) covered the common case, but a file whose declared type disagreed with its filename-inferred language, or whose logicalName went unresolved, could still sort incorrectly; separately, Vivado's component.xml generator re-resolved the fileset fallback path even when an explicit rtlFiles list was already supplied, silently discarding the caller's intended order. Both are now root-caused: a file's declared language/logical name is honored over path-based inference, and the fallback path only runs when rtlFiles is genuinely absent. (#91)

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Consistency Check: a new drift-detection feature that cross-references a .ip.yml's declared ports, clocks, resets, parameters, bus interfaces, and registers against the top-level HDL (regardless of its managed: flag) and, once scaffolded, the Platform Designer (_hw.tcl) and Vivado (component.xml) vendor artifacts. Drift surfaces as color-coded canvas annotations, a review overlay with Adopt/Regenerate/Inspect/Ignore actions and a copy-to-clipboard button, and a single amber/red "Drift" status badge in the toolbar. Runs on demand from the toolbar or IPCraft: Check Consistency, and automatically (silently, badge-only) on webview open and whenever a watched HDL source or vendor artifact changes on disk, debounced 800ms. Bus-interface and memory-map/register comparison (Vivado only, since Platform Designer's _hw.tcl carries no register data) was added in a follow-up pass. (#84, #96, #92)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Consistency Check false positives and gaps: a series of correctness fixes found while auditing the new check against every bundled example — bus-interface physical ports (reconstructed from physicalPrefix/portNameOverrides) and interrupt ports were wrongly reported as undeclared new ports; the check silently passed when the top-level HDL file had no managed: false flag at all (the schema default is managed: true); quoted VHDL/Verilog string generic and parameter defaults were flagged as mismatched against the unquoted .ip.yml value even when identical; "Keep .ip.yml & Regenerate" skipped the staging/review step that "Scaffold Project" gives; a fileSets entry the scaffold pack has no rule for (e.g. an extra hand-authored file) vanished from the Scaffold/Regenerate review list instead of showing up as protected; and the audit also uncovered pre-existing bugs in HwTclParser (silently dropping [expr ...] bracket expressions it couldn't reduce), one-sided string-quote normalization, and conduit interfaces ignoring their own physicalPrefix when computing accounted-for port names. (#93, #94)
  • Vivado component.xml import/export correctness: fixed two bugs surfaced by the new bus-interface/register comparison — portNameOverrides (per-signal renamed suffixes) were never passed through when generating component.xml, so renamed ports exported with the wrong physical names, and were never reconstructed at all when importing a component.xml; a bus interface with no common physical prefix (an empty-string prefix) lost its per-signal renames entirely on import, since the override computation only ran when a prefix was present.
  • Unsorted RTL file order in generated component.xml: the fileSets fallback path (used when explicit RTL file list isn't supplied, e.g. import-only flows) emitted files in raw declaration order instead of compile-dependency order, unlike the equivalent Quartus _hw.tcl fallback — could place a register file before its package, causing simulation errors. (#91)
  • Memory map indicator not opening for a per-interface memoryMapRef: the canvas click-to-open handler for a bus interface's memory-map indicator only resolved the global memoryMaps: { import } form, never the array-of-named-maps form (memoryMaps: [{ name, import }]) written when a map is attached to a specific bus interface — clicking the indicator silently did nothing. (#95)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Generate Documentation: a new standalone command and toolbar button that renders a full Markdown IP datasheet (docs/<name>_datasheet.md) covering overview, parameters, ports, bus interfaces, clocks/resets, and the register map. IPCraft: Scaffold Project now also emits the datasheet by default, gated by the new ipcraft.generate.includeDocs setting. (#87)
  • Optional IP author field: a new author field on the IP core, shown in the canvas Inspector's Details section and as a third block-header subtitle (visible only when set); flows into generated file headers and Platform Designer's legacy AUTHOR property. (#86)
  • Report Issue / Send Feedback button: a feedback button in the IP Core editor toolbar and the Memory Map editor sidebar strip opens VS Code's native issue reporter (pre-filled with extension/VS Code/OS versions), and the same action is now offered alongside "Show Logs" whenever an error notification is shown. No GitHub token or secrets are stored in the extension — submission happens through the user's browser. (#85)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ipcraft CLI: a new standalone ipcraft command-line tool (npx ipcraft generate ...) that runs the same generator as the extension without needing VS Code or a built extension source tree. (#72)
  • ipcraft verify: regenerates a .ip.yml in memory and diffs it against what's actually committed in a generated directory, listing every stale or missing file and exiting non-zero on drift — a CI/pre-commit gate for "generated output matches the current spec". (#73)
  • IPCraft: Check HDL Consistency (managed:false): cross-references a .ip.yml's declared ports/clocks/resets/parameters against its managed: false top-level HDL. (#74)
  • fileSets entries marked managed: false that collide with a scaffold target are now never (re)generated, even on the very first run, instead of only once the file already exists on disk. (#75)
  • simulation.topLevel in .ip.yml now overrides the generated cocotb testbench's TOPLEVEL (e.g. to point at a board wrapper), defaulting to the IP core's own name. (#78)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Quartus HDL input-version misconfiguration: quartus_project.tcl unconditionally emitted a VHDL-2008 input-version assignment even for pure-SystemVerilog designs, which Quartus 23.1std rejects for mixed/SV-only projects. Now derives VHDL/SV presence from the actual RTL file list and emits the correct assignment(s) — VERILOG_INPUT_VERSION SYSTEMVERILOG_2005 for SV, VHDL_INPUT_VERSION VHDL_2008 for VHDL, or both for mixed-language designs. (#76)
  • Bus-less generated output hygiene: _hw.tcl no longer claims an "Avalon-MM slave interface for register access" in its header comment for components with no memory-mapped slave (e.g. clock + reset + one conduit), and the generated Quartus SDC no longer emits derive_pll_clocks for designs with no PLL instantiated — both were previously unconditional. (#77)
  • HDL Consistency Check and ipcraft verify refinements: a file listed in more than one fileSet no longer produces duplicate findings; when several managed: false HDL files exist, only the one whose entity/module name matches the IP core's name is checked against the full port/clock/reset/parameter list (falling back to checking every file when the top-level can't be identified), so a hand-authored submodule that doesn't expose the top-level interface no longer produces false missing-port findings; ipcraft verify now also scans for files left behind in a directory after a --target is dropped (previously invisible, since the scan only walked directories the current invocation's target list touches); and a schema-invalid .ip.yml with an undefined name can no longer spuriously "match" an unparseable HDL file as the top-level.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Hardware-validated example projects (examples/): three full IPCraft-generated example projects — a minimal Avalon-MM LED peripheral, and register/field-access conformance suites over Avalon-MM and AXI4-Lite — validated end-to-end on real DE10-Nano hardware. They double as generator regression fixtures.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• SLVERR not returned for unmapped AXI-Lite reads: the generated AXI-Lite bus wrapper's register bank asserted rd_valid on every rd_en regardless of address validity, so the SLVERR path was dead code and reads to unmapped addresses returned RRESP=OKAY with zero data instead of RRESP=SLVERR. Fixed in both the VHDL and SystemVerilog templates to match the already-correct write-response behavior. (Fixes #59)
  • Reset-value overflow and WORD-addressed Avalon-MM slave bugs: a 32-bit resetValue at or above 0x80000000 overflowed VHDL's signed 32-bit integer/natural default type and failed GHDL elaboration; fixed by emitting a fixed-width bit-string literal instead. Separately, an Avalon-MM slave whose address port is narrowed via portWidthOverrides (for Nios II-compatible WORDS addressing) produced an out-of-range VHDL slice; fixed by zero-padding instead of slicing, with a companion fix so the generated _hw.tcl correctly declares addressUnits WORDS to match.
  • Stale RTL files leaking into vendor packaging on a language switch: regenerating an IP in a different ipcraft.generate.hdlLanguage than its existing fileSets entries (e.g. re-running in SystemVerilog when fileSets still names .vhd files) pulled the stale files back in alongside the freshly generated ones, corrupting the resulting Makefile/component.xml/Vivado/Quartus project scripts. fileSets-declared paths are now deduplicated against freshly generated output by path stem, ignoring extension.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Packaged .vsix no longer includes dev-only files (build/, docker/, Jenkinsfile, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) or the .test-fixtures//examples/ directories, reducing package size.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Bus interface clock/reset routing matrix: a new clickable "Ports" header on the IP Core canvas (positioned below the Generics/Dependencies sections, mirroring the existing Generics overview) opens a matrix panel listing every bus interface with inline Clock/Reset dropdowns and a hover-to-delete action, plus a separate Resets section showing each reset's own associated clock — so clock/reset routing can be audited and fixed across the whole core without clicking through each interface individually. (#57)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Parameterized port widths lost their function/generic on VHDL and Verilog import: extractWidthFromType/extractWidth only recognized a predefined width function (clog2, log2, ceil, floor, min, max) when its argument was a bare parameter name. A function applied to an arithmetic expression on a generic — e.g. clog2(DW/2) — matched none of the import patterns: the Verilog importer dropped the width entirely (silently falling back to a fixed default, losing the generic reference altogether), and the VHDL importer fell back to re-storing the raw expanded VHDL text (integer(ceil(log2(real(DW/2))))) instead of the canonical clog2(DW/2), which then failed to parse on the next regeneration and leaked VHDL-only syntax into SystemVerilog/Tcl output. Both importers now reverse-map the generator's own canonical VHDL/SystemVerilog expansions back to the width-expression form via the shared widthExprAst module, with the function argument allowed to be an arbitrary arithmetic expression. (#37)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Vivado VHDL-93/2008 misclassification: generated component.xml registered every VHDL file as plain vhdlSource, which Vivado treats as VHDL-93 when the IP is instantiated in a block design, rejecting VHDL-2008 constructs during synthesis. VHDL files now default to VHDL-2008 (userFileType vhdlSource-2008, matching Vivado's own packaging), and each file in a fileSets entry can set an explicit version (87/93/2002/2008/2019) via a new dropdown in the Source Files editor. (#28)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Master-detail block editor: the address-block screen now shows the register map alongside an inline register editor, so registers can be edited in place without leaving the block.
  • Drag-to-reorder in the outline: address blocks, top-level registers, and registers inside a register array can now be reordered by dragging their gripper handle. Moves are confined to the same sibling group and repack offsets automatically.
  • Live reorder preview: dragging a bit field or an outline node reflows the list into the prospective drop position in real time, with a theme-aware focus ring marking the item being moved (replaces the previous drop-line indicators).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Register map visualizer: register name labels stay visible when the panel is resized narrow, the register-array badges no longer crop, and the side-by-side panes are resizable.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Memory Map Structural Desync: Fixed a critical bug where array-level operations (insert, delete, drag-and-drop relocate) on Address Blocks, Registers, and Bitfields would corrupt memory address offsets and bit range allocations.
  • Memory map file corruption on rapid edits: register insertions sent two document updates back-to-back (structural edit + layout repack); the second edit could race the first in the extension host, replacing only the older document extent and leaving a stale tail of duplicated YAML. The webview now applies the edit and the repack in a single pass (one update per gesture), and DocumentManager serializes document updates per URI so overlapping edits can never use a stale replace range.
  • Spurious document changes and whole-file reformatting: clicking around the memory map view could mark the file dirty without any real edit (editors committed unchanged values on blur), and every write reserialized the entire document with js-yaml — changing indentation and deleting all comments. All memory-map writes now go through YamlService.applyPathEdits, which edits the parsed document in place (yaml Document API): no-op edits produce no update at all, untouched content keeps its formatting, comments and hex spellings, and structural edits only re-render the subtree that actually changed.
  • YAML schema pollution: whole-map and array-level writes now pass through a YamlSanitizer that strips runtime-only keys (address_offset, base_address, bit_offset/bit_width/bit_range, __kind), canonicalizes aliases to the ipcraft-spec schema spelling (baseAddress, resetValue, enumeratedValues), and drops injected defaults (size: 32, range: 4096, monitorChangeOf: null). DataNormalizer no longer fabricates range and preserves defaultRegWidth, so those values survive round-trips through the editor.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Stateless Layout Recomputation: Replaced ad-hoc manual array shifting and incremental offset math in UI components with a centralized, pure functional LayoutEngine that strictly enforces invariants top-down.
  • Mutation Service API: Re-architected structural edits across the application (in BlockEditor.tsx, RegisterMapVisualizer.tsx, and FieldOperationService.ts) to use MutationService for array state manipulations, followed by a global recomputeFullLayout pass.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• SystemVerilog generation: all scaffold and generate commands now produce .sv source files when ipcraft.generate.hdlLanguage is set to systemverilog. The scaffold command generates the full project layout (package, top, core, bus wrapper, register file) in the configured HDL language.
  • Headless build (IPCraft: Build): compiles Vivado (OOC and full XPR) and Quartus projects in batch mode from inside VS Code, without opening the GUI. Live output streams to a dedicated IPCraft Build Output Channel.
  • Build Reports panel: Explorer sidebar tree view showing WNS/WHS (Vivado) or Fmax (Quartus), LUT/FF/BRAM/DSP utilization, and CDC violations. Click any node to open the corresponding report file.
  • Status bar build indicator: shows live $(loading~spin) Building… while running; collapses to $(pass) WNS +1.23ns or $(pass) Fmax 156 MHz on success.
  • vivado_run_ooc.tcl and vivado_run_xpr.tcl scripts generated alongside the Vivado project files, allowing headless OOC synthesis and full implementation via vivado -mode batch.
  • New settings: ipcraft.quartus.shellPath (path to quartus_sh), ipcraft.build.jobs (parallel job count), and ipcraft.generate.hdlLanguage (vhdl or systemverilog).
  • Vivado project output directory changed from <ip_name>_vivado/ to build/ooc/ to keep source files clean.
  • Full bus-interface detection in VHDL parser: detectBusInterfaces now scores against all five supported bus definitions — AXI4-Full, AXI4-Lite, AXI-Stream, Avalon-MM, and Avalon-ST — using a prefix-based scoring algorithm with exclusive-signal disambiguation (e.g. awlen/wlast distinguish AXI4-Full from AXI4-Lite) and a pollution ratio check to reject false-positive matches.
  • Auto clock/reset association: when a VHDL entity has exactly one clock and one reset, the parser automatically populates associatedReset on clock entries, associatedClock on reset entries, and associatedClock/associatedReset on every detected bus interface.
  • IPCraft application menu: added a top-level IPCraft entry to the VS Code application menu bar. All file-type commands (scaffold, export, build, import) are now accessible from this menu without needing to right-click a file in the Explorer.
  • _hw.tcl source directive resolution: the Platform Designer importer now follows source directives recursively, so multi-file IP core packages are imported in full.
  • Compilation-order sorting: imported fileset files are sorted by compilation dependency order (packages before entities, entities before architectures) when scaffolding from existing source.

docs.title: Contributing Guidelines
docs.text:
IPCraft keeps two change records:

  • CHANGELOG.md at the repository root holds the user-facing release notes. It ships in the VSIX and is shown on the Marketplace, so write its entries in user terms: what users can now do or what no longer goes wrong, without module names, internal refactors, CI or test changes. Put changes that need action on upgrade (different generated output, schema or pack compatibility) under Before you upgrade.
  • The developer changelog is the technical record for contributors, with modules, issues and pull requests, including internal work.

Record every notable change in the developer changelog; add a release-notes entry as well when users will notice it.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
See Development setup for supported tools, debugging, and repository structure.

ipcraft-spec (bus definitions and JSON schemas) is a git submodule. After cloning:

git submodule update --init --recursive
npm install

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a branch from your target base branch
  2. Make focused changes
  3. Add/update tests
  4. Run lint/type-check/tests
  5. Open a PR with a clear summary

docs.title: Local Validation Checklist
docs.text: Run lint, type check, unit tests, and a compile before opening a pull request, plus the suites that cover your change. Testing lists the commands and which suite to choose.

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
Use concise, action-focused messages with conventional prefixes:

Prefix Purpose feat: New functionality fix: Bug fix docs: Documentation only test: Test additions/updates refactor: Code reshaping without behavior change chore: Maintenance/tooling

Examples:

  • fix: clear field table drafts after reorder
  • test: add useFieldEditor reorder synchronization regression

docs.title: Code Guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep changes scoped to the problem
  • Prefer pure functions for algorithms/services
  • Preserve existing naming and style conventions
  • Avoid any; use unknown + type guards when needed
  • Update docs if behavior or workflow changes

docs.title: Frontend Patterns
docs.text:
• Keep components focused and composable
  • Move complex interaction logic into hooks/services
  • Keep YAML mutation path centralized through resolver/service flow

docs.title: Extension Host Patterns
docs.text:
• Use provider/service boundaries
  • Keep message contracts explicit and simple
  • Avoid direct webview/business coupling in providers

docs.title: Testing Expectations
docs.text: Add or update tests for bug fixes (a regression test), algorithm changes, and hook or service behavior changes. See Testing for where each kind of test lives.

docs.title: Pull Requests
docs.text:
Include in PR description:

  1. What changed
  2. Why it changed
  3. How it was validated (commands + results)
  4. Any known follow-up work

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js 20+ and npm
  • VS Code 1.80 or later
  • Python 3 (optional — needed only for docs_* targets)
  • CMake 3.20+ (optional — provides a unified build interface, see below)

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Use npm for normal extension development. Use CMake when you want the same cross-language target names used by automation or documentation tasks; both paths run the same underlying npm commands.

CMake (recommended)npm 

cmake -B build          # configure once
cmake --build build --target setup
setup runs npm install → generate-types → compile in sequence.

npm install
npm run generate-types   # regenerate TypeScript types from JSON schemas
npm run compile

Launch the Extension Development Host with F5.

docs.title: VS Code Compatibility Policy
docs.text:
The minimum supported version is declared by engines.vscode in package.json. The @types/vscode dependency is pinned exactly to that version so extension code cannot compile against a newer API by accident. npm run type-check verifies that the two declarations remain aligned.

npm run test:e2e runs against the declared minimum by default. To exercise another release explicitly, compile the extension and tests, then set VSCODE_TEST_VERSION:

npm run compile
npm run compile-tests
VSCODE_TEST_VERSION=stable npm run test:e2e

CI runs the extension-host smoke suite against both the declared minimum and the current stable release. Raise the minimum only when the extension intentionally uses a newer API, and update engines.vscode and the exact @types/vscode version together.

docs.title: Architecture at a Glance
docs.text:
IPCraft runs in two JavaScript environments that communicate through postMessage:

  • The extension host runs in Node.js and owns VS Code APIs, files, commands, importers, generation, and vendor tools.
  • The webviews run in embedded browsers and render the Memory Map, IP Core, Data Inspector, and system diagram React applications.

The main entry points are src/extension.ts, src/webview/index.tsx, src/webview/ipcore/IpCoreApp.tsx, src/webview/dataInspector/index.tsx, and src/webview/systemDiagram/index.tsx; the command line starts in src/cli/. Start with Architecture Overview before changing the message boundary.

docs.title: Repository Layout
docs.text:
src/
  extension.ts              # extension entry point
  cli/                      # ipcraft command line
  commands/                 # VS Code command implementations
  providers/                # custom editor providers and panels
  services/                 # extension host services (incl. systemDiagram/)
  domain/                   # normalized types shared by host and webviews
  yamledit/                 # comment-preserving YAML edits
  parser/                   # VHDL, Verilog, _hw.tcl, component.xml, system design readers
  generator/                # scaffolder, resolvers, Nunjucks templates, scaffold packs
  dataInspector/            # bit vectors, literals, recipes, capture readers
  shared/                   # code used by both host and webviews
  sidebar/                  # IP core tree view
  utils/                    # logging, error handling, helpers
  webview/                  # React apps: Memory Map, IP Core, Data Inspector, system diagram
  test/                     # unit, browser, e2e, and integration tests
config/                     # Jest, webpack, Playwright, and other tool configuration
resources/                  # icons and static assets
scripts/                    # build, screenshot, and maintenance scripts
docs/                       # this documentation
ipcraft-spec/               # specification schemas and examples (git submodule)

docs.title: Build, Lint, Type Check
YAML Editing Rule
docs.text:
IPCraft deliberately uses two YAML libraries:

Library Use js-yaml v4 Read-only parsing or simple output where formatting preservation is irrelevant yaml v2 Any modify-and-write-back path that must preserve comments and numeric spellings

Format-preserving writes go through src/yamledit/ (applyPathEdits, applyPathDeletes). Do not introduce a js-yaml dump into an editor write-back path.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: See Testing for the test suites and which to run. With CMake, cmake --build build --target test, test_coverage, test_browser, test_e2e, and test_all run the same suites.

docs.text:
cmake --build build --target vsix

npx vsce package

See Building a VSIX Package for the full workflow including version bumps and installation.

docs.title: Extension Host
docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: Common Development Tasks
docs.text: Good first contributions include focused unit-test improvements, validation messages, small component fixes, and documentation corrections. Keep changes narrow and add a regression test when fixing behavior.

docs.title: Add a new command
docs.text:
1. Implement in src/commands/*
  2. Register in src/extension.ts
  3. Add command contribution in package.json

docs.title: Add a memory map feature
docs.text:
1. UI behavior in the relevant component or hook
  2. Algorithm in src/webview/algorithms/ or service in src/webview/services/
  3. Tests in src/test/suite/
  4. Update docs

docs.title: Add generator behavior
docs.text:
1. Update src/generator/* and templates in src/generator/templates/*
  2. VHDL templates use *.vhdl.j2 suffix; SystemVerilog templates use *.sv.j2; vendor templates follow altera_*.j2 and amd_*.j2 naming
  3. Register new templates in TemplateLoader if needed
  4. Validate with sample specs in ipcraft-spec/examples/*
  5. Update the Generator Reference

docs.title: Add an IP Core canvas feature
docs.text:
The IP Core editor has no sidebar/section-tabs mode — editing happens on the block-diagram canvas plus its Inspector panel. See IP Core Editor Reference.

  1. Add a draggable entry to src/webview/ipcore/components/canvas/LibraryPalette.tsx if the feature introduces a new droppable primitive
